title.raw: 卷40 陸俟 Volume 40: Lu Si

sentences.zh: 陸俟，代人也。

translations.literal: Lu Si was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖幹，祖引，世領部落。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Gan, his grandfather Yin; for generations they led their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gan and his grandfather Yin had led their tribal group for generations.

sentences.zh: 父突，太祖時率部民隨從征伐，數有戰功，拜厲威將軍、離石鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Tu, in the time of Emperor Daozu, led tribal followers in campaigns; he repeatedly achieved merit in battle and was appointed General of Stern Prestige and Military Commander of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tu had led their tribesmen on campaign under Emperor Daozu, won repeated battlefield honors, and been appointed General of Stern Prestige and military commander of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 天興中，為上黨太守、關內侯。

translations.literal: During the Tianxing era, he served as Administrator of Shangdang and Marquis of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing reign he held the posts of Shangdang prefect and Marquis of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 俟少聰慧，有策略。

translations.literal: Si from youth was clever and resourceful, possessed of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Lu Si was clever and shrewd, with a gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐阼，拜侍郎，遷內侍，襲爵關內侯，轉龍驤將軍、給事中，典選部蘭臺事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan ascended the throne, [Si] was appointed Gentleman Attendant; he was promoted to Inner Attendant, inherited the title Marquis of Guannei, transferred to General of the Dragon Chargers and Palace Attendant, and oversaw the selection office and Orchid Terrace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan came to the throne, Lu Si was named Gentleman Attendant, then promoted to inner attendant, inherited the Marquisate of Guannei, and was made General of the Dragon Chargers and Palace Attendant in charge of the personnel selection office and Orchid Terrace records.

sentences.zh: 當官而行，無所屈橈。

translations.literal: He acted according to office in performance of duty, yielding nowhere to pressure.
translations.idiomatic: In office he did his duty without bending to pressure.

sentences.zh: 世祖親征赫連昌，詔俟督諸軍鎮大磧，以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu personally campaigned against Helian Chang, he ordered Si to supervise the armies garrisoning the Great Desert to guard against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu marched in person against Helian Chang, he ordered Lu Si to command the armies holding the Great Desert against possible Rouran attack.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，復典選部蘭臺事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, [Si] again oversaw the selection office and Orchid Terrace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned, Lu Si again took charge of the selection office and Orchid Terrace records.

sentences.zh: 與西平公安頡督諸軍攻虎牢，克之，賜爵建業公，拜冀州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: Together with Prince of Xiping An Tjie he supervised the armies in attacking Hulao, captured it, was granted the ducal title Duke of Jianye, appointed Governor of Jizhou, and retained his former generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince of Xiping An Tjie in commanding the armies that took Hulao; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianye, appointed governor of Jizhou, and kept his former rank as general.

sentences.zh: 時考州郡治功，唯俟與河內太守丘陳為天下第一。

translations.literal: When the achievements of prefectures and districts in governance were assessed, only Si and Qiu Chen, Administrator of Henei, ranked first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial and commandery administrations were graded, only Lu Si and Qiu Chen, prefect of Henei, ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 轉都督洛豫二州諸軍事、本將軍、虎牢鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise all military affairs of the two provinces Luo and Yu, retained his former generalship, and became Great General of the Garrison at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to command all military affairs in Luozhou and Yuzhou as before, with his former rank as general, and made great garrison commander at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 平涼休屠金崖、羌狄子玉等叛，復轉為使持節、散騎常侍、平西將軍、安定鎮大將。

translations.literal: When Jin Ya of Xiutu in Pingliang, Ziyu of the Qiang Di, and others rebelled, he was again transferred to Credential-Holder, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General Who Pacifies the West, and Great General of the Garrison at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin Ya of the Xiutu people in Pingliang, Ziyu of the Qiang Di, and others rose in revolt, he was again appointed envoy with imperial staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the west, and great commander of the Anding garrison.

sentences.zh: 既至，懷柔羌戎，莫不歸附。

translations.literal: Having arrived, he won over the Qiang and Rong with kindness; none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he won over the Qiang and other frontier peoples with kindness, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 追討崖等，皆獲之。

translations.literal: Pursuing and attacking Ya and the others, all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued Ya and his fellows and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 徵還，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was named regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出為平東將軍、懷荒鎮大將。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Great General of the Garrison at Huaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as general who pacifies the east and great commander of the Huaihuang garrison.

sentences.zh: 未期，諸高車莫弗訟俟嚴急，待下無恩，還請前鎮將郎孤。

translations.literal: Before his term was complete, the various chieftains (mofu) of the Gaoche sued, saying Si was harsh and severe, showed no kindness to subordinates, and asked that the former garrison commander Lang Gu be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term was up, the Gaoche chieftains petitioned that Lu Si was overly harsh and graceless toward his men, and they asked for the return of the former commander Lang Gu.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔許之，徵俟還京。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu by edict granted this and summoned Si back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu approved the request and recalled Lu Si to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至朝見，言於世祖曰：「陛下今以郎孤復鎮，以臣愚量，不過周年，孤身必敗，高車必叛。

translations.literal: Having arrived and been received in audience, he said to Emperor Taiwu: "Your Majesty now restores Lang Gu to the garrison; by my dull reckoning, within no more than a year Lang Gu alone will be defeated and the Gaoche will surely rebel."
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he told Emperor Taiwu, "If Your Majesty restores Lang Gu to the garrison, in my judgment within a year he will be ruined and the Gaoche will rebel."

sentences.zh: 」世祖疑謂不實，切責之，以公歸第。

translations.literal: " The emperor doubted that this was true, sharply rebuked him, and sent the duke back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor doubted him, rebuked him sharply, and sent him home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸莫弗果殺郎孤而叛。

translations.literal: The next year, the various mofu indeed killed Lang Gu and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the chieftains did kill Lang Gu and rise in revolt, just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，大驚，即召俟，問其知敗之意。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu heard of it, he was greatly startled and immediately summoned Si, asking the meaning of his foreknowledge of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu heard this he was astonished and at once summoned Lu Si to ask how he had foreseen the disaster.

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「夫高車上下無禮，無禮之人，難為其上。

translations.literal: Si said: "The Gaoche from high to low lack propriety; men without propriety are hard to govern from above.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si said, "Among the Gaoche there is no propriety between high and low; people without propriety are hard to rule from above.

sentences.zh: 臣所以莅之以威嚴，節之以憲網，欲漸加訓導，使知分限。

translations.literal: Therefore I governed them with stern majesty and restrained them with the legal net, wishing gradually to add instruction and guidance so they would know their bounds.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I governed them with stern authority and restrained them by law, hoping gradually to teach them their proper limits.

sentences.zh: 而惡直醜正，實繁有徒，故訟臣無恩，稱孤之美。

translations.literal: Yet those who hate the upright and detest the correct are indeed many in number; hence they sued that I had no kindness and praised Gu's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: But those who hate the upright and resent discipline are many; they accused me of lacking kindness and praised Lang Gu.

sentences.zh: 孤獲還鎮，欣其名譽，必加恩於百姓，譏臣為失，專欲以寬惠治之，仁恕待之。

translations.literal: Gu, having regained the garrison, delighted in his reputation, was sure to heap favor on the common people, mocked me as mistaken, and intended solely to govern them with lenient kindness and treat them with benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lang Gu returned to command, pleased with his reputation, he was bound to shower favors on the people, mock my methods as wrong, and try to rule only through leniency and indulgence.

sentences.zh: 無禮之人，易生陵傲，不過期年，無復上下，然後收之以威，則人懷怨懟，怨懟既多，敗亂彰矣。

translations.literal: Men without propriety easily breed arrogance and insolence; within no more than a year there would again be no distinction of high and low; then when he tried to rein them in with stern authority, people would harbor resentment and anger; once resentment and anger were many, defeat and disorder would become manifest.
translations.idiomatic: People without propriety soon grow arrogant; within a year there would be no order of rank at all. When he then tried to restore authority by force, resentment would pile up—and widespread resentment brings defeat and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」世祖笑曰：「卿身乃短，慮何長也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taiwu laughed and said: "Your body is short—how long your foresight!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "You are short in stature, but how far you see ahead!"

sentences.zh: 」即日，復除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " That same day he was again appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Lu Si was reappointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世祖征蠕蠕，破涼州，常隨駕別督輜重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Rouran and broke Liang Province, [Si] constantly followed the imperial carriage in separately supervising baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaigns against the Rouran and the conquest of Liangzhou, he often accompanied the emperor in a separate command over the supply trains.

sentences.zh: 又與高涼王那渡河南，略地至濟南東平陵，徙其民六千家於河北。

translations.literal: Again, together with Prince of Gaoliang Na, he crossed south of the Yellow River, raided as far as Dongpingling in Jinan, and moved six thousand households of its people north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He also crossed the Yellow River with Prince of Gaoliang Na, raided as far as Dongpingling in Jinan, and resettled six thousand households north of the river.

sentences.zh: 又以俟都督秦雍二州諸軍事、平西將軍、長安鎮大將。

translations.literal: Again Si was made to supervise all military affairs of the two provinces Qin and Yong, General Who Pacifies the West, and Great General of the Garrison at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si was again appointed to command all military affairs in Qinzhou and Yongzhou, as general who pacifies the west and great commander of the Chang'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 與高涼王那擊蓋吳於杏城，大破之。

translations.literal: Together with Prince of Gaoliang Na he attacked Gai Wu at Xingcheng and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Gaoliang Na he attacked Gai Wu at Xingcheng and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 獲吳二叔，諸將欲送京師，俟獨不許，曰：「夫長安一都，險絕之土，民多剛強，類乃非一。

translations.literal: They captured Wu's two uncles; the generals wished to send them to the capital, but Si alone would not permit it, saying: "Chang'an is a capital city, a land of extreme strategic strength; its people are mostly tough and unyielding, and their kinds are not one.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Gai Wu's two uncles; the other generals wanted to send them to the capital, but Lu Si alone objected, saying, "Chang'an is a capital in rugged country; its people are tough, and they are not all of one kind.

sentences.zh: 清平之時，仍多叛動，今雖良民，猶以為懼，況其黨與乎？

translations.literal: Even in times of peace there were still many rebellions; now, though they are good common people, they will still be afraid—how much more his partisans?
translations.idiomatic: Even in peaceful times there were frequent uprisings; though the people are loyal now, they will still be afraid—how much more his followers?

sentences.zh: 若不斬吳，恐長安之變未已。

translations.literal: If Wu is not beheaded, I fear the troubles of Chang'an will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we kill Gai Wu, I fear unrest in Chang'an will never end.

sentences.zh: 吳一身藏竄，非其親信，誰能獲之？

translations.literal: Wu alone is in hiding; who but his close confidants can capture him?
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu is in hiding alone; who but his own trusted men can catch him?

sentences.zh: 若停十萬之眾以追一人，非上策也。

translations.literal: If we halt a host of a hundred thousand to pursue one man, that is not a superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: To hold a hundred thousand men idle while chasing one fugitive is no good strategy.

sentences.zh: 不如私許吳叔，免其妻子，使自追吳，擒之必也。

translations.literal: Better secretly to promise Wu's uncles, spare their wives and children, and have them pursue Wu themselves—then capture is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Better to promise his uncles privately, spare their wives and children, and let them hunt him down themselves—we are sure to take him.

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸曰：「今來討賊，既破之，獲其二叔，唯吳一人，何所復至。

translations.literal: " All the generals said: "We came now to punish the rebel; having already defeated him and captured his two uncles, with only Wu as one man—what further trouble can there be?"
translations.idiomatic: " The generals all said, "We came to crush the rebel; we have beaten him and taken his two uncles—what harm can one man, Gai Wu, still do?"

sentences.zh: 」俟曰：「吳之悖逆，本自天性，今若獲免，必誑惑愚民，稱王者不死，妄相扇動，為患必大。

translations.literal: " Si said: "Wu's perversity and rebellion spring from his very nature; if he now escapes punishment, he is sure to deceive and beguile the foolish common people, claiming that one who would be king does not die, recklessly stirring them up—the harm will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Si replied, "Gai Wu's treason is in his nature; if he goes free he will delude the common people, claim that a would-be king cannot die, and stir up trouble on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 諸君不見毒蛇乎？

translations.literal: Have you gentlemen not seen a venomous serpent?
translations.idiomatic: Have you never seen a venomous snake?

sentences.zh: 斷其頭猶能為害，況除腹心疾，而曰必遺其類，其可乎？

translations.literal: Cut off its head and it can still do harm—how much more when removing a disease of the heart and belly, yet saying one must surely leave its kind—can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: Cut off its head and it can still strike; how much less can you cure a disease at the heart and say you must leave its kind alive—is that reasonable?

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: " The generals said: "The duke's words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals said, "My lord is right.

sentences.zh: 但得賊不殺，更有所求，遂去不返，其如罪何？

translations.literal: But if we obtain the rebel yet do not kill him, and he has further demands and then goes away and does not return—what of the crime?"
translations.idiomatic: But if we spare the rebel and he makes new demands and never comes back—how will we answer for the offense?"

sentences.zh: 」俟曰：「此罪我與諸君當之。

translations.literal: " Si said: "For this crime I and you gentlemen will answer."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Si said, "I and you gentlemen will bear that blame together."

sentences.zh: 」高涼王那亦從俟計，遂遣吳二叔，與之期。

translations.literal: " Prince of Gaoliang Na also followed Si's plan; they then sent off Wu's two uncles and made an agreement with them.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince of Gaoliang Na agreed to Lu Si's plan; they released Gai Wu's two uncles and set a deadline with them.

sentences.zh: 及吳叔不至，諸將各咎於俟。

translations.literal: When Wu's uncles did not arrive, each of the generals blamed Si.
translations.idiomatic: When the uncles failed to return, every general blamed Lu Si.

sentences.zh: 俟曰：「此未得其便耳，必不背也。

translations.literal: Si said: "They have not yet found the opportune moment—that is all; they will surely not break faith."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si said, "They have not yet found the right moment; they will not betray us."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，果斬吳以至，皆如其言。

translations.literal: " Several days later they indeed beheaded Wu and brought [his head]; all was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later they did bring Gai Wu's head, exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 俟之明略獨決，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Si's clear insight and independent decisions were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si's foresight and decisive judgment were always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 遷內都大官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Officer of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand officer of the inner capital.

sentences.zh: 安定盧水劉超等聚黨萬餘以叛，[1]世祖以俟威恩被於關中，詔以本官加都督秦雍諸軍事，鎮長安。

translations.literal: Liu Chao of the Lushui in Anding and others gathered a party of more than ten thousand and rebelled;[1] Emperor Taiwu, because Si's prestige and kindness extended through Guanzhong, ordered him with his former office additionally to supervise all military affairs of Qin and Yong and garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao of the Lushui people in Anding and others raised a band of more than ten thousand in revolt.[1] Because Lu Si's authority and kindness were felt throughout Guanzhong, Emperor Taiwu ordered him to keep his present rank, take command of all military affairs in Qin and Yong, and hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「秦川險絕，奉化日近，吏民未被恩德，故頃年已來，頻有叛動。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu said: "Qinchuan is strategically strong and isolated; submission to our rule is recent; officials and people have not yet received imperial grace—hence in recent years there have been frequent rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qinchuan is rugged and hard to reach; our rule there is still new, and the officials and people have not yet felt imperial kindness—hence the repeated uprisings in recent years.

sentences.zh: 今超等恃險，不順王命，朕若以重兵與卿，則超等必合而為一，據險拒戰，未易攻也；

translations.literal: Now Chao and the others rely on the terrain's strength and do not obey the royal command; if I give you a heavy force, then Chao and the others will surely unite as one, hold the strategic ground and resist in battle—it will not be easy to attack;
translations.idiomatic: Now Chao and his fellows trust the terrain and defy the throne. If I give you a large army, they will unite, hold the passes, and be hard to defeat;

sentences.zh: 若以輕兵與卿，則不制矣。

translations.literal: if I give you a light force, then you cannot control them."
translations.idiomatic: if I give you too few men, you cannot control them at all."

sentences.zh: 今使卿以方略定之。

translations.literal: Now I send you to settle it by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: I am sending you to settle this by strategy alone."

sentences.zh: 」於是俟單馬之鎮，超等聞之大欣，以為無能為也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Si went to the garrison alone on horseback; when Chao and the others heard of it they were greatly pleased, thinking he could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Si then rode to his post alone. When Chao and his men heard this they were delighted, thinking he could do nothing against them.

sentences.zh: 既至，申揚威信，示以成敗，誘納超女，外若姻親。

translations.literal: Having arrived, he proclaimed and displayed his prestige and authority, showed them success and failure, enticed and received Chao's daughter, and outwardly treated them as if by marriage kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he displayed his authority, showed them the consequences of victory and defeat, won over Chao's daughter in marriage, and treated them outwardly like kin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 超猶自警，初無降意。

translations.literal: Chao still kept himself on guard; at first he had no intention of surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: Chao remained wary and at first had no thought of surrender.

sentences.zh: 俟乃率其帳下，往見超，觀其舉措，設掩襲之計。

translations.literal: Si then led his personal attendants, went to see Chao, observed his movements, and devised a plan for a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si then took his personal guard to visit Chao, studied his habits, and laid a plan for a surprise strike.

sentences.zh: 超使人逆曰：「三百人以外，適當以弓馬相待，三百人以內，當以酒食相供。

translations.literal: Chao sent a man to meet him and say: "Beyond three hundred men, we should properly meet with bow and horse; within three hundred men, we should supply wine and food."
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent word ahead: "If you bring more than three hundred men, we shall meet you with arms; if three hundred or fewer, we shall receive you with food and wine."

sentences.zh: 」俟乃將二百騎詣超，超設備甚嚴。

translations.literal: " Si then led two hundred horsemen to visit Chao; Chao made his preparations very strict.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Si went with two hundred horsemen. Chao made elaborate preparations.

sentences.zh: 俟遂縱酒盡醉而還。

translations.literal: Si then gave himself to wine, drank to complete drunkenness, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Si drank freely until he was thoroughly drunk, then rode back.

sentences.zh: 後謂將士曰：「超可取也。

translations.literal: Afterward he told his officers and soldiers: "Chao can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told his officers, "Chao can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」乃密選精兵五百人，陳國恩德，激厲將士，言至懇切。

translations.literal: " He then secretly selected five hundred elite troops, set forth the state's grace and virtue, and roused the officers and soldiers, speaking with utmost earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: " He secretly chose five hundred picked troops, spoke to them of the state's kindness, and stirred them with words of deep earnestness.

sentences.zh: 士卒奮勇，各曰：「以死從公，必無二也。

translations.literal: The soldiers were spirited and brave; each said: "We will follow my lord unto death—assuredly with no second thought."
translations.idiomatic: The men took fire; each said, "We will follow you to the death—there will be no second thought."

sentences.zh: 」遂偽獵而詣超，與士卒約曰：「今會發機，當以醉為限。

translations.literal: " They then feigned a hunt and went to Chao; with the soldiers he agreed: "When the moment comes to strike, drunkenness shall be the signal."
translations.idiomatic: " They pretended to go hunting and approached Chao. He told his men, "When we strike, let drunkenness be our signal."

sentences.zh: 」俟於是詐醉，上馬大呼，手斬超首。

translations.literal: " Si then feigned drunkenness, mounted his horse with a great shout, and with his own hand beheaded Chao.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Si then pretended to be drunk, mounted, shouted, and with his own hand cut off Chao's head.

sentences.zh: 士卒應聲縱擊，殺傷千數，遂平之。

translations.literal: The soldiers at the sound charged forth in attack; those killed and wounded numbered in the thousands, and the rebellion was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His men charged at once; they killed and wounded thousands and the rebellion was pacified.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悅，徵俟還京師，轉外都大官，散騎常侍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu was greatly pleased, summoned Si back to the capital, transferred him to Grand Officer of the Outer Capital, and he remained Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was delighted, recalled Lu Si to the capital, made him grand officer of the outer capital, and left him regular attendant of the scattered cavalry as before.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，以子麗有策立之勳，拜俟征西大將軍，進爵東平王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, because his son Li had merit in the stratagem of establishing him, Si was appointed General Who Campaigns West and advanced in rank to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng came to the throne, because his son Li had helped plan his accession, Lu Si was named general who campaigns west and advanced to Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 太安四年薨，年六十七，諡曰成。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taian he died, aged sixty-seven; his posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taian, at sixty-seven; his posthumous name was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 有子十二人。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons.

sentences.zh: 長子馛，多智，有父風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ba was greatly intelligent and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ba was very clever and took after his father.

sentences.zh: 高宗見馛而悅之，謂朝臣曰：「吾常歎其父智過其軀，是復踰於父矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng saw Ba he was pleased with him and said to the court ministers: "I have often sighed that his father's wisdom exceeded his stature; this one again surpasses his father."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng met Ba he took a liking to him and told the court, "I used to marvel that his father's mind outran his frame; this son surpasses his father again."

sentences.zh: 」少為內都下大夫，奉上接下，行止取與，每能逆曉人意，與其從事者無不愛之。

translations.literal: " In youth he was Junior Grand Master of the Inner Capital; in serving superiors and receiving subordinates, in conduct, bearing, taking and giving, he could each time anticipate others' intentions in advance; none who worked with him failed to love him.
translations.idiomatic: " While young he served as junior grand master of the inner capital. In dealing with superiors and subordinates alike, in every gesture of giving and receiving, he could read people's minds in advance, and all who worked with him loved him.

sentences.zh: 興安初，賜爵聊城侯，出為散騎常侍、安南將軍、相州刺史，假長廣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xing'an he was granted the marquisate of Liaocheng, went out as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Xiang Province, with the provisional title Duke of Changgung.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xing'an era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liaocheng and sent out as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the south, and governor of Xiangzhou, with the provisional title Duke of Changgung.

sentences.zh: 為政清平，抑強扶弱。

translations.literal: In governing he was clear and fair, restraining the strong and supporting the weak.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was fair and peaceful; he curbed the powerful and helped the weak.

sentences.zh: 州中有德宿老名望重者，以友禮待之，詢之政事，責以方略。

translations.literal: Within the province there were virtuous elders of long standing and heavy reputation; he treated them with the rites due to friends, inquired of them on affairs of government, and charged them with stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the province's most respected elders as friends, consulted them on policy, and held them accountable for counsel.

sentences.zh: 如此者十人，號曰「十善」。

translations.literal: There were ten such men, called the "Ten Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: There were ten such men, known as the "Ten Worthies."

sentences.zh: 又簡取諸縣強門百餘人，以為假子，誘接殷勤，賜以衣服，令各歸家，為耳目於外。

translations.literal: Again he selected from the various districts more than a hundred men of powerful clans, made them his foster sons, enticed and received them with earnest attentiveness, bestowed clothing on them, ordered each to return home, and used them as eyes and ears outside.
translations.idiomatic: He also chose more than a hundred men from powerful local families across the prefecture, took them as foster sons, treated them warmly and gave them clothes, then sent each home to serve as his eyes and ears in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 於是發姦摘伏，事無不驗。

translations.literal: Thereupon in exposing wrongdoing and uncovering hidden crimes, nothing failed to be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Through this network he exposed crime and hidden guilt, and nothing failed to check out.

sentences.zh: 百姓以為神明，無敢劫盜者。

translations.literal: The common people regarded him as numinous and divine; none dared to rob or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The people thought him almost supernatural, and no one dared rob or steal.

sentences.zh: 在州七年，家至貧約。

translations.literal: During seven years in the province, his household was extremely poor and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in office his household remained extremely poor and austere.

sentences.zh: 徵為散騎常侍，民乞留馛者千餘人。

translations.literal: When he was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, more than a thousand common people begged that Ba be kept.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to serve as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, more than a thousand people petitioned to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 顯祖不許，謂羣臣曰：「馛之善政，雖復古人何以加之？

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen would not permit it and said to the assembled ministers: "Ba's excellent governance—even the ancients, how could one add to it?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen refused and told his ministers, "Ba's good government—even the ancients could hardly have done better."

sentences.zh: 」賜絹五百匹、奴婢十口。

translations.literal: " He granted five hundred bolts of silk and ten household slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk and ten servants.

sentences.zh: 馛之還也，吏民大斂布帛以遺之，馛一皆不受，民亦不取，於是以物造佛寺焉，名長廣公寺。

translations.literal: When Ba returned, officials and common people greatly gathered cloth and silk to present to him; Ba refused every gift, and the people also would not take them back; thereupon with the goods they built a Buddhist temple, named the Temple of Duke Changgung.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure officials and people raised a great collection of cloth and silk as a parting gift. Ba refused it all, and when the donors would not take it back either, the goods were used to build a Buddhist temple called the Temple of Duke Changgung.

sentences.zh: 後襲父爵，改封建安王。

translations.literal: Later he inherited his father's noble rank and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited his father's title and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 時劉彧司州刺史常珍奇以懸瓠內附，而新民猶懷去就。

translations.literal: At that time Chang Zhenqi, Governor of Sizhou under Liu Yu, submitted Xuangu from within, yet the newly submitted people still harbored thoughts of staying or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chang Zhenqi, Liu Yu's governor of Sizhou, surrendered Xuangu to Wei, but the newly submitted population still wavered between staying and leaving.

sentences.zh: 馛銜旨撫慰，諸有陷軍為奴婢者，馛皆免之。

translations.literal: Ba carried out the imperial order to comfort and reassure them; all who had been taken captive by the army and made slaves and maidservants—Ba freed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ba carried out the imperial commission to reassure them, and freed everyone who had been enslaved after falling into military hands.

sentences.zh: 百姓忻悅，民情乃定。

translations.literal: The common people were glad and pleased, and popular sentiment was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The people were delighted, and public sentiment settled.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕犯塞，車駕親討，詔馛為選部尚書，錄留臺事，督兵運糧，一委處分。

translations.literal: When the Rouran violated the frontier and the imperial carriage personally campaigned against them, an edict made Ba Minister of the Selection Department, recording affairs of the capital left behind, supervising troops and transporting grain—everything was entrusted to his disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier and the emperor marched in person, Ba was ordered to serve as minister of the selection department, oversee capital affairs in the emperor's absence, and command troop movements and grain transport—with full discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 顯祖將禪位於京兆王子推，任城王雲、隴西王源賀等並皆固諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was about to abdicate the throne in favor of Prince Tui of Jingzhao; Prince of Rencheng Yun, Prince of Longxi Yuan He, and others all firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen planned to abdicate in favor of Prince Tui of Jingzhao, Prince of Rencheng Yun, Prince of Longxi Yuan He, and others all strongly objected.

sentences.zh: 馛抗言曰：「皇太子聖德承基，四海屬望，不可橫議，干國之紀。

translations.literal: Ba spoke out in opposition, saying: "The crown prince's sagely virtue inherits the foundation; the four seas look to him—one must not rashly debate and violate the state's statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Ba spoke up boldly: "The crown prince's virtue upholds the foundation of the state, and the realm looks to him. Such reckless talk must not be allowed to violate the nation's laws."

sentences.zh: 臣請刎頸殿庭，有死無貳。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to cut his throat in the palace hall—there is death but no second loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to cut my throat here in the hall—I will die rather than waver."

sentences.zh: 」久之，帝意乃解，詔曰：「馛，直臣也，其能保吾子乎！

translations.literal: " After a long while the emperor's mind was relieved; an edict said: "Ba is a straight minister—can he not protect my son!"
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while the emperor relented and said by edict, "Ba is an upright minister—surely he can protect my son!"

sentences.zh: 」遂以馛為太保，與太尉源賀持節奉皇帝璽紱，傳位于高祖。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ba was made Grand Tutor; together with Grand Marshal Yuan He, bearing the imperial staff, they presented the emperor's seal and cord and transferred the throne to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed Ba grand tutor. Together with Grand Marshal Yuan He, bearing the imperial staff, they presented the imperial seal and cord and transferred the throne to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 延興四年薨，贈以本官，諡曰貞王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died; he was posthumously granted his former office, and his posthumous title was Prince Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died; he was posthumously granted his former rank and given the posthumous title Prince Zhen.

sentences.zh: 馛有六子，琇、凱知名。

translations.literal: Ba had six sons; Xiu and Kai were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Ba had six sons; Xiu and Kai were the ones who became well known.

sentences.zh: 琇，字伯琳，馛第五子。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Bolin, was Ba's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, whose courtesy name was Bolin, was Ba's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 母赫連氏，身長七尺九寸，甚有婦德。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Helian clan; her height was seven feet nine inches, and she possessed excellent womanly virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a woman of the Helian clan, seven feet nine inches tall, and widely admired for her womanly virtue.

sentences.zh: 馛有以爵傳琇之意。

translations.literal: Ba had the intention of passing the title on to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ba intended to pass the family title on to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 琇年九歲，馛謂之曰：「汝祖東平王有十二子，我為嫡長，承襲家業，今已年老，屬汝幼沖，詎堪為陸氏宗首乎？

translations.literal: When Xiu was nine years old, Ba said to him: "Your grandfather the Prince of Dongping had twelve sons. I am the eldest legitimate son and inherited the family estate. Now I am old, and you are still young—how could you serve as head of the Lu clan?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was nine, Ba said to him, "Your grandfather, the Prince of Dongping, had twelve sons. I am the eldest legitimate son and inherited the family estate. I am old now, and you are still a child—how could you bear the burden of leading the Lu clan?"

sentences.zh: 」琇對曰：「苟非鬬力，何患童稚。

translations.literal: Xiu replied: "If it is not a matter of physical strength, what need is there to worry about being young?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu replied, "If the issue is not brute strength, why should youth be a concern?"

sentences.zh: 」馛奇之，遂立琇為世子。

translations.literal: Ba marveled at this and thereupon established Xiu as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was impressed and thereupon named Xiu his heir.

sentences.zh: 馛薨，襲爵。

translations.literal: When Ba died, [Xiu] inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba died, Xiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 琇沉毅少言，雅好讀書，以功臣子孫為侍御長、給事中，遷黃門侍郎，轉太常少卿、散騎常侍、太子左詹事、領北海王師、光祿大夫，轉祠部尚書、司州大中正。

translations.literal: Xiu was deep and resolute, spoke little, and elegantly loved reading. As a descendant of meritorious officials he served as Chief of the Imperial Attendants and Gentleman at the Gate, was promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant, transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors, Left Mentor to the Crown Prince, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Beihai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, transferred to Minister of Rites, and Grand Rectifier of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was grave, resolute, and sparing of speech, with a refined love of books. As the descendant of a meritorious house he served as chief of the imperial attendants and gentleman at the gate, was promoted to yellow gate attendant, then vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices, regular attendant of the privy counselors, left mentor to the crown prince, and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Beihai, grand master of splendid happiness, minister of rites, and grand rectifier of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 會從兄叡事免官。

translations.literal: About that time his older cousin Rui was implicated in a matter and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: About that time his older cousin Rui was caught up in a scandal and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 景明初，試守河內郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, he was put on probation as administrator of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, he was appointed provisional administrator of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧謀反，令子曇和與尹仵期、薛繼祖等先據河內。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion and ordered his son Tanhe, together with Yin Wuqi, Xue Jizu, and others, to seize Henei first.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion and sent his son Tanhe, together with Yin Wuqi, Xue Jizu, and others, to seize Henei first.

sentences.zh: 琇聞禧敗，斬曇和首。

translations.literal: When Xiu heard that Xi had been defeated, he beheaded Tanhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu learned that Xi had been defeated, he cut off Tanhe's head.

sentences.zh: 時以琇不先送曇和，禧敗始斬首，責其通情，徵詣廷尉。

translations.literal: At the time it was held that because Xiu had not sent Tanhe in advance but only beheaded him after Xi's defeat, he was charged with collusion and summoned to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court held that Xiu had failed to surrender Tanhe beforehand and had only beheaded him after Xi's defeat; he was accused of collusion and summoned to the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 廷尉少卿崔振窮治罪狀，按琇大逆，陸宗大小，咸見收捕。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Zhen exhaustively investigated the charges; indicting Xiu for treason, all members of the Lu clan, great and small, were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhen, vice director of the court of judicial review, pursued the case to the end; charging Xiu with treason, he had every member of the Lu clan, high and low, arrested.

sentences.zh: 會將赦，先薨於獄。

translations.literal: Just as an amnesty was about to be issued, he died in prison first.
translations.idiomatic: Just as an amnesty was about to be proclaimed, he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 琇弟凱仍上書訴冤，世宗詔復琇爵。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Kai still submitted a memorial pleading innocence, and Emperor Xuanwu by edict restored Xiu's title.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Kai continued to submit memorials pleading his brother's innocence, and Emperor Xuanwu issued an edict restoring Xiu's title.

sentences.zh: 子景祚襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingzuo inherited [the title].
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 凱，字智君，謹重好學。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Zhijun, was careful, serious, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, whose courtesy name was Zhijun, was cautious, dignified, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 年十五，為中書學生，拜侍御中散，轉通直散騎侍郎，遷太子庶子、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At fifteen he became a student at the Secretariat, was appointed Attendant Cavalryman-in-Attendance, transferred to Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors on Direct Service, and promoted to Companion to the Crown Prince and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the secretariat school, was appointed attendant cavalryman-in-attendance, transferred to regular attendant of the privy counselors on direct service, and was promoted to companion to the crown prince and gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 凱在樞要十餘年，以忠厚見稱，希言屢中，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Kai was in key positions for more than ten years, was praised for loyalty and honesty, and his rare remarks often hit the mark; Emperor Xiaowen commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai held key posts for more than ten years and was praised for loyalty and integrity; his rare comments often proved prescient, and Emperor Xiaowen commended him.

sentences.zh: 後遇患，頻上書乞骸骨，詔不許，敕太醫給湯藥。

translations.literal: Later he fell ill and repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement; the edict did not permit it but ordered the imperial physicians to supply medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell ill and repeatedly asked leave to retire; the emperor refused, but ordered the imperial physicians to provide him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 除正平太守，在郡七年，號為良吏。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Zhengping; during seven years in the commandery he was acclaimed as a good official.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Zhengping and, over seven years in the commandery, earned a reputation as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖將議革變舊風，大臣並有難色。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xiaowen was about to discuss reforming old customs, the high ministers all showed difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen first proposed reforming old customs, the senior ministers all looked uneasy.

sentences.zh: 又每引劉芳、郭祚等密與規謨，共論時政，而國戚謂遂疏己，怏怏有不平之色。

translations.literal: Moreover he often secretly summoned Liu Fang, Guo Zuo, and others to plan together and discuss current affairs, while the imperial kinsmen felt they were being neglected and showed discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He also frequently summoned Liu Fang, Guo Zuo, and others in private to plan reforms and discuss state affairs, while the imperial kinsmen felt themselves sidelined and grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 乃令凱私喻之曰：「至尊但欲廣知前事，直當問其古式耳，終無親彼而相疏也。

translations.literal: So [the emperor] had Kai privately explain to them: "His Majesty only wishes to broaden his knowledge of past affairs; he should simply ask about ancient norms—he will not in the end favor them and treat you coldly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore had Kai explain privately to them, "His Majesty only wants to learn more about earlier practices; he is simply asking about old precedents. In the end he will not favor them and turn away from you."

sentences.zh: 」國戚舊人意乃稍解。

translations.literal: The minds of the imperial kinsmen and old officials were gradually relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kinsmen and veteran officials gradually felt reassured.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧謀逆，凱兄琇陷罪，凱亦被收，遇赦乃免。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion, Kai's elder brother Xiu was implicated in crime; Kai was also arrested but was released when an amnesty was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion, Kai's elder brother Xiu was implicated; Kai was arrested as well but was released when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 凱痛兄之死，哭無時節，目幾失明，訴冤不已，備盡人事。

translations.literal: Kai grieved his brother's death, wept at all hours, nearly went blind, ceaselessly pleaded innocence, and exhausted every possible means.
translations.idiomatic: Kai mourned his brother's death, weeping at all hours until his eyes nearly failed; he never stopped pleading Xiu's innocence and exhausted every avenue open to him.

sentences.zh: 至正始初，世宗復琇官爵，凱大喜，置酒集諸親曰：「吾所以數年之中抱病忍死者，顧門戶計耳。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Zhengshi era, Emperor Xuanwu restored Xiu's offices and title. Kai was greatly delighted, set out wine, and gathered his kin, saying: "The reason I endured illness and clung to life these many years was for the sake of our family standing."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengshi era, Emperor Xuanwu restored Xiu's offices and title. Overjoyed, Kai set out wine and gathered his relatives, saying, "The reason I endured illness and clung to life all these years was for the sake of our family's standing."

sentences.zh: 逝者不追，今願畢矣。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be recovered; now my wish is fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: What is gone cannot be brought back—but now my wish is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」遂以其年卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died that same year.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 贈龍驤將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Southern Qing Province, with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title General of the Flying Dragon and inspector of Southern Qing Province, with the posthumous name Hui (Kind).

sentences.zh: 長子暐，字道暉，與弟恭之並有時譽。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei, styled Daohui, together with his younger brother Gongzhi, both enjoyed contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wei, courtesy name Daohui, and his younger brother Gongzhi both enjoyed great contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令賈禎見其兄弟，歎曰：「僕以老年，更覩雙璧。

translations.literal: When Luoyang Magistrate Jia Zhen saw the brothers, he sighed: "I am already old, yet again I behold a pair of jade disks."
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Zhen, magistrate of Luoyang, met the brothers, he sighed, "I am old now, yet here again I see a pair of jade disks."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗兄弟共候黃門郎孫惠蔚，惠蔚謂諸賓曰：「不意二陸復在座隅，吾德謝張公，無以延譽。

translations.literal: On another occasion the brothers together called on Yellow Gate Gentleman Sun Huiwei; Huiwei said to the guests: "I did not expect the two Lus to be here again in the corner. My virtue falls short of Duke Zhang's—I have no way to spread their praise."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the brothers called together on Sun Huiwei, gentleman of the yellow gate. Sun said to the other guests, "I did not expect to find the two Lus here again in the corner. My virtue falls short of Duke Zhang's—I have no way to do justice to their reputations."

sentences.zh: 」暐起家司徒行參軍，太尉西閣祭酒，兼尚書右民、三公郎，坐事免。

translations.literal: Wei began his career as Aide to the Grand Minister of Education, Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Grand Marshal, concurrently Right Secretary for the People and Gentleman of the Three Dukes; he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Wei began his career as an aide in the grand minister of education's office, libationer of the grand marshal's western pavilion, and concurrently right secretary for the people and gentleman of the three dukes; he was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後除伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Quells the Waves.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed general who quells the waves.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Zhengguang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengguang era.

sentences.zh: 贈司州治中。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Aide to the Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the post of aide to the inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，重贈冠軍將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Xiaochang era, he was again posthumously awarded General of the Champion and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he received a further posthumous award as general of the champion and inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 暐擬急就篇為悟蒙章，及七誘、十醉、章表數十篇。

translations.literal: Wei modeled the Literacy Primer to compose Awakening the Dull Chapter, as well as Seven Enticements, Ten Intoxications, and several dozen memorials and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei modeled his work on the Literacy Primer to write Awakening the Dull, along with Seven Enticements, Ten Intoxications, and several dozen memorials and petitions.

sentences.zh: 暐與恭之晚不睦，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: Wei and Gongzhi were on bad terms in their later years and were scorned by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Gongzhi fell out in their later years and were scorned by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 子元規，武定中，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuangui was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing during the Wuding era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuangui served as a gentleman of the masters of writing during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 恭之，字季順，有操尚。

translations.literal: Gongzhi, styled Jishun, possessed firm principles and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi, courtesy name Jishun, was a man of firm principles and integrity.

sentences.zh: 釋褐侍御史、著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the hemp, he served as Attending Censor and Aide in the Bureau of History.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering official service he was appointed attending censor and aide in the bureau of history.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除中書侍郎，領著作郎，尋除河北太守，轉征虜將軍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Director of the Bureau of History; soon after he was made Administrator of Hebei, then transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was appointed vice director of the secretariat and concurrently director of the bureau of history; soon afterward he became administrator of Hebei, then was transferred to general who subdues the barbarians and inspector of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，拜廷尉卿，加鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review and additionally made General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign of the Former Deposed Emperor he was appointed director of the court of judicial review and additionally made general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 所歷並有聲績，後坐事免。

translations.literal: In every post he achieved distinction; later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he won a strong reputation; later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，還復本任，出除征南將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was restored to his former post, then appointed General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Eastern Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was restored to his former post, then was appointed general who campaigns south and inspector of Eastern Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 天平四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、吏部尚書、定州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors, General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Inspector of Ding Province, with the posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded regular attendant of the privy counselors, general of the guard, minister of personnel, and inspector of Ding Province, with the posthumous name Yi (Dignified).

sentences.zh: 恭之所著文章詩賦凡千餘篇。

translations.literal: Gongzhi's composed essays, poems, and rhapsodies totaled more than a thousand pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi's essays, poems, and rhapsodies numbered more than a thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 子曄，開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Ye was Aide for Military Affairs in the Grand Governor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye served as aide for military affairs in the grand governor's office.

sentences.zh: 馛弟石跋，涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Shiba was Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger brother Shiba served as inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 石跋弟歸，東宮舍人、駕部校尉。

translations.literal: Shiba's younger brother Gui was Attendant of the Eastern Palace and Colonel of the Chariot Section.
translations.idiomatic: Shiba's younger brother Gui served as attendant of the eastern palace and colonel of the chariot section.

sentences.zh: 歸弟尼，內侍校尉、東陽鎮都將。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Ni was Colonel of the Inner Attendants and Commandant of Dongyang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Ni served as colonel of the inner attendants and commandant of Dongyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 尼弟麗，少以忠謹入侍左右，太武特親昵之。

translations.literal: Ni's younger brother Li, from youth served loyally and carefully at the emperor's side; Emperor Taiwu especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's younger brother Li entered service at a young age as a loyal and careful attendant at the emperor's side; Emperor Taiwu took a special liking to him.

sentences.zh: 舉動審慎而無愆失。

translations.literal: His conduct was careful and without fault.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was cautious and he never committed a misstep.

sentences.zh: 賜爵章安子，稍遷南部尚書。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Zhang'an and was gradually promoted to Minister of the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhang'an and was gradually promoted to minister of the southern branch.

sentences.zh: 太武崩，南安王余立，既而為中常侍宗愛等所殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu died, the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was enthroned, but soon afterward was killed by the Regular Palace Attendant Zong Ai and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu died, the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was enthroned, but was soon killed by the regular palace attendant Zong Ai and his associates.

sentences.zh: 百僚憂惶，莫知所立。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were anxious and alarmed, not knowing whom to enthrone.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were panic-stricken and did not know whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 麗以高宗世嫡之重，民望所係，乃首建大義，與殿中尚書長孫渴侯、尚書源賀、羽林郎劉尼奉迎高宗於苑中，立之。

translations.literal: Li, considering the weight of Emperor Wencheng's status as legitimate heir of the era and the people's hopes resting on him, was first to establish the righteous cause; together with Palace Director Changsun Kehou, Minister Yuan He, and Gentleman of the Feathered Forest Liu Ni, he welcomed Emperor Wencheng from the park and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li, recognizing that Emperor Wencheng, as the legitimate heir of his generation, carried the people's hopes, took the lead in the righteous cause; together with Changsun Kehou, palace director, Yuan He, minister of state, and Liu Ni, gentleman of the feathered forest, he went to the imperial park to welcome Emperor Wencheng and set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 社稷獲安，麗之謀矣。

translations.literal: The altars of state were secured—this was Li's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was saved—thanks to Li's design.

sentences.zh: 由是受心膂之任，在朝者無出其右。

translations.literal: Thereby he received the trust of a right-hand man; among those at court none ranked above him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he held the emperor's closest trust; at court no one outranked him in influence.

sentences.zh: 興安初，封平原王，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xing'an, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xing'an era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan and additionally appointed general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 麗辭曰：「陛下以正統之重，承基繼業，至於奉迎守順，臣職之常，豈敢昧冒以干大典。

translations.literal: Li declined, saying: "Your Majesty, bearing the weight of the legitimate succession, inherited the foundation and continued the enterprise. As for welcoming and guarding in loyalty, that is the constant duty of a subject—how dare I presumptuously encroach upon the great rite?"
translations.idiomatic: Li declined, saying, "Your Majesty bears the weight of the legitimate succession and has inherited the foundation of the state. Welcoming you and serving loyally is merely a subject's ordinary duty—how dare I presumptuously claim credit for a great achievement?"

sentences.zh: 」頻讓再三，詔不聽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly declined again and again; the edict would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again and again, but the emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 麗乃啟曰：「臣父歷奉先朝，忠勤著稱，今年至西夕，未登王爵。

translations.literal: Li then submitted: "My father served successive former courts, renowned for loyalty and diligence; this year he reached his western sunset without attaining princely rank."
translations.idiomatic: Li then submitted a memorial: "My father served successive emperors and was renowned for loyalty and diligence; this year he reached the end of his life without ever receiving a princely title."

sentences.zh: 臣幼荷寵榮，於分已過，愚款之情未申，犬馬之効未展，願裁過恩，聽遂所請。

translations.literal: "I from youth have borne favor and glory, already beyond my due; my sincere loyalty has not been expressed, my dog-and-horse service not yet displayed—I wish you would curtail excessive grace and allow my request."
translations.idiomatic: "I have enjoyed favor and honor since youth, already far beyond what I deserve; my sincere devotion has not yet been expressed, nor my service repaid. I beg you to restrain your excessive kindness and grant what I ask."

sentences.zh: 」高宗曰：「朕為天下主，豈不能得二王封卿父子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng said: "I am sovereign of the empire—can I not obtain two princedoms to enfeoff you and your father?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng said, "I am sovereign of the empire—surely I can find two princedoms to enfeoff you and your father."

sentences.zh: 」乃以其父俟為東平王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enfeoffed Li's father Si as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon enfeoffed Li's father Si as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 麗尋遷侍中、撫軍大將軍、司徒公，復其子孫，賜妻妃號。

translations.literal: Li was soon promoted to Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, and Duke of the Department of State; his descendants were restored [to rank], and his wife was granted a consort title.
translations.idiomatic: Li was soon promoted to palace attendant, grand general who pacifies the army, and duke of the department of state; his descendants were restored to rank, and his wife was granted a consort title.

sentences.zh: 麗以優寵既頻，固辭不受，高宗益重之。

translations.literal: Because favored treatment came so frequently, Li firmly declined and would not accept; Emperor Wencheng esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial favor came again and again, Li steadfastly refused to accept it, and Emperor Wencheng esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 領太子太傅。

translations.literal: [He] concurrently served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as grand tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 麗好學愛士，常以講習為業。

translations.literal: Li loved learning and cherished scholars, constantly making lecture and study his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Li loved learning and valued scholars, making lectures and study his constant occupation.

sentences.zh: 其所待者，皆篤行之流，士多稱之。

translations.literal: Those he treated were all men of steadfast conduct; scholars widely praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those he welcomed were all men of solid character, and scholars widely praised him.

sentences.zh: 性又至孝，遭父憂，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: In nature he was also deeply filial; upon his father's bereavement he wasted away beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was also deeply filial by nature; when his father died he mourned so severely that he wasted away beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，高宗崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, Emperor Wencheng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping, Emperor Wencheng died.

sentences.zh: 先是麗療疾於代郡溫泉，聞諱欲赴，左右止之曰：「宮車晏駕，王德望素重，姦臣若疾民譽，慮有不測之禍。

translations.literal: Earlier Li had been treating an illness at the hot springs in Dai Commandery. When he heard the mourning proclamation he wished to hurry [to court]; his attendants stopped him, saying: "The imperial carriage has halted its journey; your princely virtue and standing have always been weighty. If wicked ministers resent your popular renown, there is fear of unforeseen disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Li had earlier been taking the waters at the hot springs in Dai Commandery. When he heard the mourning proclamation he wanted to set out at once, but his attendants stopped him, saying, "The emperor is dead. Your virtue and standing have always been great. If wicked ministers resent your popularity, you may face unforeseen danger."

sentences.zh: 願少遲回，朝廷寧靜，然後奔赴，猶為未晚。

translations.literal: "We wish you would delay a little; once the court is calm, then rush to attend—it would still not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: "We beg you to wait a little. Once the court has settled, you can go—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」麗曰：「安有聞君父之喪，方慮禍難，不即奔波者！

translations.literal: Li said: "How could one hear of a lord and father's death and still worry about disaster rather than rush at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "How can one hear that one's lord and father has died and still weigh the risk of disaster instead of rushing to attend at once!"

sentences.zh: 」遂便馳赴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he galloped off immediately.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped off at once.

sentences.zh: 乙渾尋擅朝政，忌而害之。

translations.literal: Yifu Hun soon seized control of court affairs, envied him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu Hun soon seized control of the government, envied Li, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 初，渾悖傲，每為不法，麗數諍之，由是見忌。

translations.literal: Initially Hun was insolent and arrogant, constantly acting unlawfully; Li repeatedly remonstrated with him, and for this was resented.
translations.idiomatic: Hun had long been arrogant and lawless; Li repeatedly remonstrated with him, and for that earned his hatred.

sentences.zh: 顯祖甚追惜麗，諡曰簡王，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen deeply mourned and cherished Li; he was given the posthumous title Prince Jian and buried alongside [the emperor] at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen deeply mourned Li; he was given the posthumous title Prince Jian and buried at Jinling alongside the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 高祖追錄先朝功臣，以麗配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen posthumously recorded the meritorious officials of the former court and had Li share in sacrifices at the ancestral temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen later recorded the meritorious officials of the previous reign and had Li honored with a place in the ancestral temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 麗二妻，長曰杜氏，次張氏。

translations.literal: Li had two wives: the elder was the Du clan; the second was the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li had two wives: the first was of the Du clan, the second of the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 長子定國，杜氏所生；

translations.literal: The eldest son Dingguo was born to the Du clan;
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Dingguo, was born to the Du clan;

sentences.zh: 次叡，張氏所生。

translations.literal: the second, Rui, was born to the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: the second, Rui, was born to the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 子昕之，字慶始，風望端雅。

translations.literal: His son Xinzhi, styled Qingshi, had an upright and elegant reputation and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinzhi, courtesy name Qingshi, had an upright and elegant reputation.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，例降為公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title; by regulation it was reduced to that of duke.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced from princely rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 尚顯祖女常山公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xianwen's daughter, the Princess of Changshan, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Fast for the Emperor's Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Xianwen's daughter, the Princess of Changshan, and was appointed commandant of the horse fast for the emperor's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 歷通直郎，景明中，以從叔琇罪免官。

translations.literal: He served as Direct Attendant; during Jingming, because of his cousin (once removed) Xiu's crime he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as direct attendant; during the Jingming era he was dismissed from office because of the crime of his cousin Xiu.

sentences.zh: 尋以主壻，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, as the princess's husband, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors on Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as the emperor's son-in-law, he was appointed regular attendant of the privy counselors on direct service.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷司徒司馬，加輔國將軍，出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Director of the Department of State, additionally made General Who Assists the State, and sent out as Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice director of the department of state and general who assists the state, and was sent out as inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 尋進號安東將軍，治有名績，仍除青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East; his administration won noted achievements, and he was then appointed Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to general who pacifies the east; his administration won a strong reputation, and he was then appointed inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 在州著寬平之稱，轉安北將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the province he was known for lenience and fairness; he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was known for lenience and fairness; he was then transferred to general who pacifies the north and inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 永平四年夏卒。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the fourth year of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮東將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province; his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of general who pacifies the east and inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，定國娶河東柳氏，生子安保，後納范陽盧度世女，生昕之。

translations.literal: Initially, Dingguo married a woman of the Liu clan of Hedong and bore the son Anbao; afterward he took as a concubine a daughter of Lu Dushi of Fanyang and bore Xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dingguo married a woman of the Liu clan of Hedong and had a son, Anbao; later he took a daughter of Lu Dushi of Fanyang as a concubine and had Xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 二室俱為舊族而嫡妾不分。

translations.literal: Both households were old families, yet the distinction between primary wife and concubine was not observed.
translations.idiomatic: Both wives came from established clans, but no clear distinction was made between the primary wife and the concubine.

sentences.zh: 定國亡後，兩子爭襲父爵。

translations.literal: After Dingguo's death, the two sons contended to inherit their father's title.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingguo died, the two sons fought over who would inherit their father's title.

sentences.zh: 僕射李沖有寵於時，與度世子淵婚親相好。

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Chong was favored at the time and was on good terms by marriage with Yuan, son of Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Chong was influential at court and was close to Dushi's son Yuan through marriage ties.

sentences.zh: [2]沖遂左右申助，昕之由是承爵尚主，職位赫弈。

translations.literal: [2] Chong then exerted influence on both sides to assist, and Xinzhi thereby inherited the title, married an imperial princess, and held a dazzlingly prominent position.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Chong then pulled strings on his behalf, so Xinzhi inherited the title, married an imperial princess, and rose to dazzling prominence.

sentences.zh: 安保沉廢貧賤，不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Anbao sank into obscurity, poverty, and low status, unable to escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Anbao was left in obscurity and poverty, and could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 昕之容貌柔謹，高祖以其主壻，特垂昵眷。

translations.literal: Xinzhi's appearance was gentle and respectful; because he was the emperor's son-in-law, Emperor Xiaowen showed him special affectionate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi had a gentle, deferential bearing, and because he was the emperor's son-in-law, Emperor Xiaowen showed him exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，年未四十，頻撫三蕃，當世以此榮之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizong's reign, though not yet forty, he frequently governed the three frontier garrisons, and his contemporaries counted this an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong, though still under forty, he was repeatedly appointed to govern the three frontier regions, which contemporaries regarded as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 昕之卒後，母盧悼念過哀，未幾而亡。

translations.literal: After Xinzhi died, his mother Lu mourned with excessive grief and before long passed away herself.
translations.idiomatic: After Xinzhi died, his mother Lu grieved so deeply that she soon followed him in death.

sentences.zh: 公主奉姑有孝稱，神龜初，與穆氏頓丘長公主並為女侍中。

translations.literal: The princess served her mother-in-law with filial devotion and won repute for it; at the beginning of Shengui, she and the Princess of Dunqiu of the Mu clan were both made female palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The princess cared for her mother-in-law with filial devotion and won praise for it; at the beginning of the Shengui era she and Lady Mu, Princess of Dunqiu, were both appointed female palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 又性不妬忌，以昕之無子，為納妾媵，而皆育女。

translations.literal: Moreover, by nature she was free of jealousy; because Xinzhi had no sons, she took concubines for him, yet all bore daughters.
translations.idiomatic: She was also free of jealousy; since Xinzhi had no sons, she found concubines for him, but they all bore daughters.

sentences.zh: 公主有三女無男，以昕之從兄希道第四子子彰為後。

translations.literal: The princess had three daughters and no sons, so she made Zizhang, fourth son of Xinzhi's cousin Sidao, her heir.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had three daughters and no son, so she adopted Zizhang, the fourth son of Xinzhi's cousin Sidao, as her heir.

sentences.zh: 子彰，字明遠，本名士沈。

translations.literal: Zizhang, styled Mingyuan, original name Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang, courtesy name Mingyuan, was originally named Shishen.

sentences.zh: 年十六出後，事公主盡禮。

translations.literal: At sixteen he became an adopted heir and treated the princess with full propriety.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was made heir to their line and served the princess with complete propriety.

sentences.zh: 丞相高陽王雍嘗言曰：「常山妹雖無男，以子彰為兒，乃過自生矣。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Prince Yong of Gaoyang once said: "Though the younger sister of Changshan has no sons, taking Zizhang as her son surpasses bearing one herself.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Prince Yong of Gaoyang once said, "Though the Princess of Changshan had no son of her own, in taking Zizhang as her heir she did better than if she had borne one herself.

sentences.zh: 」 正光中，襲爵東郡公，尋除散騎侍郎，拜山陽太守。

translations.literal: " During Zhenguang, he inherited the title of Duke of Dongjun; soon he was made Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Prefect of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era he inherited the title of Duke of Dongjun, was soon appointed gentleman of the scattered cavalry, and became prefect of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，徵拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi came to the throne, he was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi took the throne, Zizhang was summoned and appointed attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 子彰妻即咸陽王禧女。

translations.literal: Zizhang's wife was a daughter of Prince Xi of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang's wife was a daughter of Prince Xi of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 禧誅，養於彭城王第，莊帝親之，略同諸姊。

translations.literal: When Xi was executed, she was raised in the household of Prince Cheng of Peng, and Emperor Zhuangdi treated her with affection much as he did his elder sisters.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi was executed, she was raised in the household of Prince Cheng of Peng, and Emperor Zhuangdi treated her with nearly the same affection as his elder sisters.

sentences.zh: 建義初，尒朱榮欲修舊事，庶姓封王，由是封子彰濮陽王，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Erzhu Rong wished to restore the old practice of ennobling commoners as kings, and for this reason enfeoffed Zizhang as Prince of Puyang with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, Erzhu Rong sought to revive the old practice of ennobling men of common lineage as kings, and so enfeoffed Zizhang as Prince of Puyang with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋而詔罷，仍復先爵。

translations.literal: Before long an edict revoked this, and he recovered his former title.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon revoked the ennoblement, and he reverted to his previous title.

sentences.zh: 除安西將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the west and inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 還，拜征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，領廣平王贊開府諮議參軍事。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Golden Sign and Purple Punctuation, and also served as counselor on the staff of Prince Zan of Guangping's household.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed general who pacifies the east and grand master of golden sign and purple punctuation, and served as staff counselor to Prince Zan of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 天平中，拜衞將軍、潁州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he was appointed General of the Guard and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was appointed general of the guard and inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 元象中，以本將軍除齊州刺史，又加驃騎將軍，行懷州事。

translations.literal: During Yuanxiang, with his existing rank as general he was appointed Inspector of Qi Province, additionally made General of Chivalry and Cavalry, and charged with affairs of Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanxiang era he was appointed inspector of Qi Province with his existing general's rank, promoted to general of chivalry and cavalry, and charged with administering Huai Province.

sentences.zh: 轉北豫州刺史，仍除徐州刺史，將軍並如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of North Yu Province, then also appointed Inspector of Xu Province, his generalships remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of North Yu Province and then also appointed inspector of Xu Province, retaining his general's titles.

sentences.zh: 一年歷三州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: In one year he held three provinces in succession, and his contemporaries counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he held three provincial posts in succession, which his contemporaries regarded as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除衞大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of the Privy Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed grand general of the guard and left grand master of the privy counselors.

sentences.zh: 又行瀛州事。

translations.literal: He was also charged with affairs of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with administering Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 復行滄州事。

translations.literal: He again took charge of affairs in Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He again took charge of affairs in Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 進號驃騎大將軍，行冀州事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Chivalry and Cavalry and charged with affairs of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of chivalry and cavalry and charged with administering Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 除侍讀、兼七兵尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lecturer Attendant and concurrently Minister of the Seventh Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed lecturer attendant and concurrently minister of the seventh armies.

sentences.zh: 行青州事。

translations.literal: He was charged with affairs of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with administering Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 子彰之為州，以聚斂為事，晚節修改，自行青、冀、滄、瀛，甚有時譽，加以虛己納物，人敬愛之。

translations.literal: When Zizhang held provincial office, he made enrichment his business; in his later years he reformed his ways, and from the time he personally governed Qing, Ji, Cang, and Ying he won great contemporary reputation; moreover, by humbling himself and accepting counsel he earned people's respect and affection.
translations.idiomatic: In his early provincial career Zizhang was given to enrichment, but in later years he changed his ways; from his terms governing Qing, Ji, Cang, and Ying he won wide contemporary praise, and by modesty and openness to others he earned respect and affection.

sentences.zh: 武定八年二月，除中書監。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Wuding, he was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year of Wuding he was appointed supervisor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三月卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the third month he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 賻帛一百匹，追贈都督青光齊三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、青州刺史，公如故，諡曰文宣。
