translations.literal: One hundred bolts of burial silk were granted; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Qing, Guang, and Qi Provinces, General of Chivalry and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies with an Opening Office, and Inspector of Qing Province; his ducal title remained as before; his posthumous title was Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred bolts of burial silk were granted. He was posthumously appointed commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Qing, Guang, and Qi provinces, general of chivalry and cavalry, equal in honor to the three excellencies with an opening office, and inspector of Qing Province, while retaining his ducal title; his posthumous name was Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 子彰崇好道術，曾嬰重疾，藥中須桑螵蛸，子彰不忍害物，遂不服焉。

translations.literal: Zizhang revered and favored the Way and its arts; he once fell gravely ill, and the medicine required mantid egg cases; Zizhang could not bear to harm living things, and so refused to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang was devoted to Daoist arts. Once, when he fell gravely ill, his prescription required mantid egg cases, but he could not bear to harm living creatures and refused to take the medicine.

sentences.zh: 其仁恕如此。

translations.literal: Such was his kindness and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his kindness and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 教訓六子，雅有法度。

translations.literal: He instructed and disciplined his six sons with proper standards throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He raised and disciplined his six sons with consistent propriety.

sentences.zh: 子昂，武定中，中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Ang, during Wuding, was Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang served as secretary of the secretariat during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 昂弟駿，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Jun was Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's younger brother Jun was groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 駿弟杳，尚書倉部郎。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Yao was Director of the Granaries Section in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Yao was director of the granaries section in the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 叡，字思弼。

translations.literal: Rui, styled Sibie.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, courtesy name Sibie.

sentences.zh: 其母張氏，字黃龍，本恭宗宮人，以賜麗，生叡。

translations.literal: His mother was the Zhang clan, styled Huanglong; originally a palace woman of Emperor Gong, she was given to Li and bore Rui.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was of the Zhang clan, styled Huanglong; originally a palace woman of Emperor Gong, she was given to Li and bore Rui.

sentences.zh: 麗之亡也，叡始十餘歲，襲爵撫軍大將軍、平原王。

translations.literal: When Li died, Rui was just over ten; he inherited the title of General Who Stabilizes the Army and Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li died, Rui was just over ten years old and inherited the titles of general who stabilizes the army and Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 沉雅好學，折節下士。

translations.literal: Deeply refined and fond of learning, he lowered himself to treat scholars with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and devoted to learning, he humbled himself before scholars.

sentences.zh: 年未二十，時人便以宰輔許之。

translations.literal: Before he was twenty, people of the time already predicted he would reach the highest office.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was twenty, people already spoke of him as a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女，[3]鑒謂所親云：「平原王才度不惡，但恨其姓名殊為重複。

translations.literal: He married a daughter of Cui Jian, Inspector of East Xu Province of Boling; [3] Jian said to those close to him: "The Prince of Pingyuan's talent and capacity are not bad, but I regret that his name and title are quite redundant.
translations.idiomatic: He married a daughter of Cui Jian, inspector of East Xu Province of Boling. [3] Jian told his intimates, "The Prince of Pingyuan's talents are not bad, but I find his personal name and princely title awkwardly redundant.

sentences.zh: 」時高祖未改其姓。

translations.literal: " At the time Emperor Xiaowen had not yet changed his surname.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen had not yet changed the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 叡婚自東徐還，經於鄴，見李彪，甚敬悅之，仍與俱趨京師，以為館客，資給衣馬僮使，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Returning from his wedding in East Xu, Rui passed through Ye, met Li Biao, greatly respected and delighted in him, and went with him at once to the capital; he made him a household retainer and provided clothes, horses, and servants, treating him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his wedding in East Xu, Rui passed through Ye, met Li Biao, and took an immediate liking to him; they traveled on together to the capital, where Rui took him on as a household retainer and provided him with clothes, horses, and servants, treating him very generously.

sentences.zh: 為北征都督，拜北部長，轉尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: As commander of the northern campaign, he was appointed Chief of the Northern Section, transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: As northern campaign commander he was appointed chief of the northern section, then director of the imperial secretariat, and additionally regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太和八年正月，叡與隴西公元琛並持節為東西二道大使，褒善罰惡，聲稱聞於京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Taihe, Rui and Yuan Chen of Longxi, both bearing imperial staffs, served as great envoys of the eastern and western routes, commending the good and punishing the wicked; their reputation reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year of Taihe, Rui and Yuan Chen of Longxi, both bearing imperial staffs, served as great envoys of the eastern and western circuits, rewarding virtue and punishing wrongdoing, and their reputation spread to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔賜叡夏服一具。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict granted Rui one set of summer garments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict granted Rui one set of summer garments.

sentences.zh: 後以叡為北征都督，擊蠕蠕，大破之。

translations.literal: Later Rui was made commander of the northern campaign, struck the Rouran, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was later appointed northern campaign commander, attacked the Rouran, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、都曹尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Central Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and director of the central personnel section.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕又犯塞，詔叡率騎五千以討之，蠕蠕遁走，追至石磧，擒其帥赤河突等數百人而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran again raided the frontier; an edict ordered Rui to lead five thousand horsemen to attack them; the Rouran fled, and he pursued them to Shiji, captured their chieftain Chihetu and several hundred others, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran again raided the frontier, an edict ordered Rui to lead five thousand horsemen against them; the Rouran fled, and he pursued them to Shiji, captured their chieftain Chihetu and several hundred of his followers, and returned.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，遷尚書左僕射，領北部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and put in charge of the Northern Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, promoted to left vice director of the imperial secretariat, and put in charge of the northern section.

sentences.zh: 十六年，降五等之爵，以麗勳著前朝，封叡鉅鹿郡開國公，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the five ranks of nobility were reduced; because Li's merit was outstanding in the previous reign, Rui was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the five ranks of nobility were reduced in grade; because Li's merit had been outstanding under the previous reign, Rui was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋為使持節、鎮北大將軍，與陽平王頤並為都督，督領軍將軍斛律桓等北征三道諸軍事，步騎十萬以討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority and General Who Pacifies the North; together with Prince Yi of Yangping he served as commander-in-chief, supervising the military affairs of the three northern routes under Campaign Generals such as Hulü Huan, with one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed bearer of the staff of authority and general who pacifies the north; together with Prince Yi of Yangping he served as overall commander, directing the three northern campaign routes under generals such as Hulü Huan, with a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 叡以下各賜衣物布帛。

translations.literal: Rui and those below him were each granted clothing and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and his subordinates were each granted clothing and cloth.

sentences.zh: 高祖親幸城北，訓誓羣帥。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen personally visited the north of the city and instructed and admonished the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen personally went to the north of the city to instruct and exhort the commanders.

sentences.zh: 除尚書令、衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the imperial secretariat and general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 叡大破蠕蠕而還。

translations.literal: Rui routed the Rouran utterly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rui routed the Rouran completely and returned.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂解令。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of mourning for his mother, he resigned the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned the directorship to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖將有南伐之事，以本官起之，改授征北將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was about to launch a southern campaign; he recalled Rui to his former office and changed his appointment to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was planning a southern campaign; he recalled Rui to his former post and reassigned him as general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 叡固辭，請終情禮。

translations.literal: Rui firmly declined, asking to fulfill his filial mourning to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Rui firmly declined, asking to complete his mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「叡猶執私痛，致違往旨，金革方馳，何宜曲遂也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Rui still clings to private grief and thereby violates the prior instruction; military affairs are pressing—how can his wish be indulged?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Rui still clings to private grief in defiance of our earlier command. Military affairs are urgent—how can we indulge his wish?

sentences.zh: 加領衞尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally put in charge of the Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally put in charge of the commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 可重敕有司，速令敦喻。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices be again instructed to urge him promptly.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices are again instructed to press him to comply at once.

sentences.zh: 」後除使持節、都督恒肆朔三州諸軍事、本將軍、恒州刺史，行尚書令。

translations.literal: " Later he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Heng, Si, and Shuo Provinces, with his existing rank as general, and Inspector of Heng Province, acting as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Heng, Si, and Shuo provinces, with his existing rank as general and as inspector of Heng Province, while acting as director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖大考百官，奪叡尚書令祿一周。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen conducted a great evaluation of officials and stripped Rui of one year's salary as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen conducted a major review of officials, Rui was deprived of one year's salary as director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，叡表曰：「臣聞先天有弗違之略，後天有順時之規。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Rui submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that Heaven has a strategy that may not be disobeyed, and the later sage has rules for following the times.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Rui submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that the plan ordained by Heaven must not be set aside, and that the wise ruler who comes after must have rules for acting in accord with the times.

sentences.zh: 今蕭鸞盜有名目，竊據江左，惡盈罪稔，天人棄之。

translations.literal: Now Xiao Luan has usurped a nominal title and stolen possession of the lands east of the Yangzi; his evil is full and his crimes ripe, and Heaven and men alike have abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiao Luan has stolen a title and seized the lands east of the Yangzi; his wickedness is complete and his crimes are ripe, and both Heaven and men have turned from him.

sentences.zh: 取亂攻昧，誠在茲日。

translations.literal: To take advantage of disorder and strike a benighted foe—truly the day is this day.
translations.idiomatic: To strike when the realm is in disorder and the enemy is in darkness—truly the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 愚以長江浩蕩，彼之巨防，可以德招，難以力屈。

translations.literal: In my humble view, the Yangzi is vast and flowing; their great barrier can be won by virtue but is hard to overcome by force.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view the Yangzi runs vast and deep; it is their great barrier, one that may be overcome by moral appeal but is hard to break by force alone.

sentences.zh: 又南土昏霧，暑氣鬱蒸，師人經夏，必多疾病。

translations.literal: Moreover, the southern lands are dim with mist, and the hot, steamy summer air makes it inevitable that troops spending the season there will suffer many illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the south is shrouded in humid mists, and the steamy summer heat makes it inevitable that armies campaigning through the season will suffer widespread sickness.

sentences.zh: 而鼎遷草創，庶事甫爾，臺省無論政之館，府寺靡聽治之所，百僚居止，事等行路，沉雨炎陽，自成癘疫。

translations.literal: Yet the dynasty is newly transplanted and all affairs have only just begun; the Secretariat and provincial offices have no halls for deliberating on government, and the ministries and courts have no places for hearing cases; the hundred officials dwell as if on the road, and soaking rain and blazing sun of themselves breed plague.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynasty has only just moved its capital and every affair is still in its first beginnings; the secretariat and provincial offices have no halls for conducting government, and the ministries and courts have no offices for hearing cases; officials live as if on the open road, and drenching rains and scorching sun breed plague by themselves.

sentences.zh: 且兵徭並舉，聖王所難。

translations.literal: Moreover, to raise troops and corvée labor together is what even a sage king finds difficult.
translations.idiomatic: And to wage war and impose corvée labor at the same time is what even a sage king finds hard to manage.

sentences.zh: 今介冑之士，外攻讎寇；

translations.literal: Now armored warriors attack the enemy abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Now armored warriors are fighting the enemy abroad;

sentences.zh: 羸弱之夫，內動土木；

translations.literal: frail men stir up earth and timber within;
translations.idiomatic: frail men are hauling earth and timber at home;

sentences.zh: 運給之費，日損千金。

translations.literal: the cost of transport and supply loses a thousand in gold each day.
translations.idiomatic: and the cost of transport and supply bleeds a thousand in gold each day.

sentences.zh: 驅罷弊之兵，討堅城之虜，將何以取勝乎？

translations.literal: To drive exhausted troops against solid-walled barbarians—by what means will victory be won?
translations.idiomatic: With what hope of victory can we drive exhausted troops against an enemy behind stout walls?

sentences.zh: 陛下往冬之舉，政欲曜武江漢，示威衡湘，自春幾夏，理宜釋甲。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's campaign last winter was meant to display martial glory on the Jiang and Han and show power on the Heng and Xiang; from spring nearly to summer, it would be fitting to lay down arms.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's campaign last winter was meant to display martial might on the Jiang and Han and show force on the Heng and Xiang; from spring nearly through summer, it is fitting to lay down arms.

sentences.zh: 願櫜旌卷斾，為持久之方；

translations.literal: I wish that the banners be stowed and the standards furled, and a strategy of endurance adopted;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the banners be furled and a long-term strategy adopted;

sentences.zh: 崇成帝居，深重本之固。

translations.literal: that the imperial residence be greatly strengthened and the foundation deeply secured.
translations.idiomatic: that the imperial residence be greatly strengthened and the foundations of rule made secure.

sentences.zh: 聖懷無內念之虞，兆庶休斤板之役，修禮華區，諷風洛浦。

translations.literal: Then the sage heart will be free of inward cares, the myriad people will be spared hammer-and-board corvée, ceremonial order will be cultivated in the central regions, and moral influence spread beside the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Majesty will be free of inward anxieties, the people will be spared corvée hammer-work, rites will be restored in the heartland, and moral influence spread along the Luo.

sentences.zh: 然簡英略之將，任猛毅之雄，南取荊湘，據其要府，則梁秦以西覩機自服；

translations.literal: Then select commanders of outstanding talent and appoint fierce, resolute heroes; take Jing and Xiang in the south and hold their key prefectures, and west of Liang and Qin all will see the opportunity and submit of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Select outstanding commanders and appoint fierce, resolute heroes; seize Jing and Xiang in the south and hold their key prefectures, and west of Liang and Qin all will see the moment and submit of themselves;

sentences.zh: 撫附振威，回麾東指，則義陽以左馳聲可制。

translations.literal: pacify, attach, and display authority, then wheel eastward, and east of Yiyang fame will run fast enough to bring control.
translations.idiomatic: pacify, reassure, and display authority, then turn east, and east of Yiyang your name alone will be enough to bring the region under control.

sentences.zh: 然後布仁化以綏近，播恩施以懷遠，凡在有情，孰不思奮！

translations.literal: Then spread benevolent transformation to settle those nearby and broadcast gracious favor to win those far off—who among all sentient beings will not burn to rise up!
translations.idiomatic: Then spread benevolent rule to settle those nearby and gracious favor to win those far off—who among all living beings will not burn to serve you!

sentences.zh: 還遣慕德之人効其餘力，乘流而下，勢勝萬倍，蕞爾閩甌，敢不稽顙！

translations.literal: Then send men who admire virtue to lend their remaining strength; sailing downstream, the momentum will be ten thousand times greater, and tiny Min and Ou—how would they dare not bow their foreheads!
translations.idiomatic: Then send men drawn by your virtue to lend their strength; sailing downstream, your momentum will be ten thousand times greater, and tiny Min and Ou—how could they fail to bow in submission!

sentences.zh: 豈必茲年，競斯寸尺。

translations.literal: Need one necessarily compete for every inch this very year?
translations.idiomatic: Must we grasp for every inch of ground in a single year?

sentences.zh: 惟願顧存近敕，納降而旋，不紆鑾輿，久臨炎暑。

translations.literal: I only wish that Your Majesty will heed the recent command, accept surrender and turn back, and not bend the imperial carriage to linger long in the scorching heat.
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that Your Majesty heed this recent counsel, accept surrender and return, and not keep the imperial carriage long in the scorching heat.

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 叡表請車駕還代，親臨太師馮熙之葬，坐削奪都督三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Rui submitted a memorial asking that the imperial carriage return to Dai and that His Majesty personally attend the funeral of Grand Preceptor Feng Xi; for this he was punished by removal of his command over the three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial asking that the imperial carriage return to Dai so the emperor could personally attend Grand Preceptor Feng Xi's funeral; for this he was stripped of his command over the three provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋除都督恒朔二州諸軍事，進號征北大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Heng and Shuo Provinces and advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Heng and Shuo provinces and promoted to general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 以有順遷之表，加邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Because of his memorial on orderly transfer, his fief was increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his memorial urging orderly withdrawal, his fief was increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時穆泰為定州刺史，辭以疾病，土溫則甚，請恒州自効，高祖許之。

translations.literal: At the time Mu Tai was Governor of Ding Province; he declined on grounds of illness, saying the climate there was too warm, and asked to serve at Heng Province instead; Emperor Xiaowen granted it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mu Tai was governor of Ding Province. He declined on grounds of illness—the climate there was too warm—and asked to serve at Heng Province instead. Emperor Xiaowen granted his request.

sentences.zh: 乃以叡為散騎常侍、定州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rui was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Governor of Ding Province, with his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was then appointed regular attendant of the scattered riders and governor of Ding Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 叡未發，遂與泰等同謀構逆。

translations.literal: Before Rui had set out, he conspired with Tai and others to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before Rui could depart, he joined Tai and others in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 賜死獄中，聽免孥戮，徙其妻子為遼西郡民。

translations.literal: He was granted death in prison; his wife and children were spared execution and were relocated as commoners of Liaoxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted death in prison. His wife and children were spared execution and relocated as commoners of Liaoxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔僕射李冲、領軍于烈曰：「陸叡、元丕，早蒙寵祿，位極人臣。

translations.literal: An edict addressed Vice Director Li Chong and Commander-in-Chief Yu Lie, saying: "Lu Rui and Yuan Pi, early favored with grace and emoluments, rose to the pinnacle of ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed Vice Director Li Chong and Commander-in-Chief Yu Lie: "Lu Rui and Yuan Pi were long favored with grace and emoluments and rose to the pinnacle of ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 自與卿等同受非常之詔，朕許以不死之旨，思得上下齊信，以保大義。

translations.literal: Since you received with you the extraordinary edict, I pledged that you would not die, thinking to win mutual trust above and below and preserve the grand principle.
translations.idiomatic: You and I alike received that extraordinary edict, and I pledged that you would not die, hoping to win mutual trust between sovereign and subject and preserve the grand principle.

sentences.zh: 朕於卿等常忘短棄瑕，務相含養。

translations.literal: Toward you I have constantly forgotten small faults and discarded flaws, striving to forbear and nurture one another.
translations.idiomatic: Toward you I have constantly overlooked small faults and flaws, striving to forbear and nurture you.

sentences.zh: 豈謂陸叡無心之甚，一至於斯！

translations.literal: Who would have thought Lu Rui's heedlessness could reach such a point!
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought Lu Rui's heedlessness could go so far!

sentences.zh: 乃與穆泰結禍，數圖反噬。

translations.literal: He joined Mu Tai in binding misfortune, repeatedly plotting to turn and bite.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Mu Tai in a bond of calamity and repeatedly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以朕遷洛，內懷不可，擬舉諸王，議引子恂，若斯之論，前後非一。

translations.literal: Because I moved the capital to Luoyang, he inwardly could not accept it; he planned to raise the princes and discussed bringing in my son Xun—such talk, before and after, was not once alone.
translations.idiomatic: He could not accept my move of the capital to Luoyang; he planned to raise the princes and discussed installing my son Xun—such talk was repeated again and again.

sentences.zh: 始欲推故南安王，次推陽平王，若不肯從，欲逼樂陵王。

translations.literal: At first he wished to push the former Prince of Nan'an, next the Prince of Yangping; if they would not follow, he intended to coerce the Prince of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: At first he sought to install the former Prince of Nan'an, then the Prince of Yangping; if they refused, he intended to coerce the Prince of Leling.

sentences.zh: 訕謗朝廷，書信炳然。

translations.literal: He slandered the court, and the letters are plainly evident.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered the court, and the letters bear clear witness.

sentences.zh: 事既垂就，叡以洛都休明，勸令小緩，於是之後，兩人復競。

translations.literal: When the affair was nearly complete, Rui, on grounds that the Luoyang capital was flourishing and enlightened, urged a slight delay; after that the two men again competed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was nearly complete, Rui urged a slight delay on grounds that the Luoyang capital was flourishing and enlightened; thereafter the two men quarreled again.

sentences.zh: 然猶隱而弗聞。

translations.literal: Yet I still kept it hidden and did not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I still heard nothing of it—the matter was kept hidden from me.

sentences.zh: 賴陽平王忠貞奮發，獲泰之言，便爾馳表，得使王人糾慝，恒岳無塵。

translations.literal: Thanks to the Prince of Yangping's loyal steadfastness and spirited action, he obtained Tai's words and at once sent a rushing memorial, enabling royal officers to investigate wickedness, and Heng and Yue were free of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the Prince of Yangping's loyal steadfastness and swift action, who obtained Tai's confession and at once sent an urgent memorial, enabling the court to investigate the crime so that Heng and Yue provinces remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 是以叡之愆失，處入門誅。

translations.literal: Therefore Rui's offenses warranted execution at the threshold of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore by law Rui's offenses warranted execution at the gate of his house.

sentences.zh: 朕諦尋前旨，許不盡法。

translations.literal: I carefully traced my earlier pledge and granted that the full law not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: On careful reflection of my earlier pledge, I granted that the full penalty of the law not be applied.

sentences.zh: 反逆之志，自負幽冥，違誓在彼，不關朕也。

translations.literal: The intent to rebel he bore in secret darkness; the breach of oath was on his side, not mine.
translations.idiomatic: The intent to rebel he bore in secret; the breach of oath was his, not mine.

sentences.zh: 反心逆意，既異餘犯，雖欲矜恕，末如之何。

translations.literal: A rebellious heart and perverse intent differ from other offenses; though I wished to show mercy, there was nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious intent differs from other offenses; though I wished to show mercy, nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 然猶憶先言，兼以末頗異議，聽自死別府，免厥孥戮其門，子孫永世不齒。

translations.literal: Yet still remembering my earlier words, and also because in the end he somewhat dissented, I permitted him to die by his own hand in another office, spared his wife and children execution at his gate, and barred his descendants forever from rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet remembering my earlier pledge, and also because he had expressed some dissent at the end, I permitted him to take his own life in another office, spared his wife and children execution, and barred his descendants forever from official standing.

sentences.zh: 元丕二子一弟，首為賊端，其父無人明證，理在可覩。

translations.literal: Yuan Pi's two sons and one younger brother were the first heads of the treacherous faction; no one could clearly prove it of the father, yet the reasoning is visible.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Pi's two sons and one younger brother were the ringleaders of the plot; no one could clearly prove complicity against the father, yet the inference is plain.

sentences.zh: 但以言無炳灼，隱而弗窮，以連坐應死，特恕為民。

translations.literal: But because the words were not brilliantly clear, I kept it hidden and did not pursue it fully; he should by guilt-by-association have died, but was specially spared to become a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: But because the evidence was not conclusive, I did not pursue it fully; though he should by guilt-by-association have been executed, I specially spared him to become a commoner.

sentences.zh: 朕本期有終，而彼自棄。

translations.literal: I originally expected to see this through to the end, but they abandoned themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I had intended to honor my pledge to the end, but they threw it away themselves.

sentences.zh: 卿等之間，忽及今日，違心乖念，一何可悲，故此別示，想無致怪也。

translations.literal: Among you, suddenly it has come to this day—hearts at odds and thoughts estranged, how very lamentable; hence this separate explanation, thinking you will not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: That it has come to this between us—hearts at odds and trust broken—is deeply lamentable. Hence this separate explanation; I trust you will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 謀反之外，皎如白日耳。」

translations.literal: Outside of the rebellion, it is as bright as daylight."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the rebellion itself, all is as clear as daylight."

sentences.zh: 沖、烈表曰：「臣等邀逢幸會，生遇昌辰。

translations.literal: Chong and Lie submitted a memorial saying: "We have encountered fortunate opportunity and been born in an age of prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Lie submitted a memorial: "We have encountered fortunate opportunity and been born in an age of prosperity.

sentences.zh: 才非利用，坐班位列；

translations.literal: Our talents are not fit for use, yet we sit among the ranks and offices;
translations.idiomatic: Our talents are unworthy of our posts, yet we sit among the highest ranks;

sentences.zh: 功無汗馬，猥受山河。

translations.literal: We have no sweat-of-horse merit, yet presumptuously receive fiefs of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: We have no battlefield merit, yet we presumptuously receive great fiefs.

sentences.zh: 叨忝之寵，終古無比；

translations.literal: The favor we presumptuously bear is unmatched since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: The favor we have received is unmatched since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 莫大之施，萬殞靡酬。

translations.literal: the greatest grace—ten thousand deaths could not repay it.
translations.idiomatic: the greatest grace imaginable—ten thousand deaths could not repay it.

sentences.zh: 而叡、丕識乖犬馬，心同梟獍，潛引童稚，構茲妖逆，違悖天常，罪踰萬殞。

translations.literal: Yet Rui and Pi, their understanding perverse as dogs and horses, their hearts like owls and jackals, secretly drew in the young, constructed this monstrous treason, violated heaven's constant order, and their guilt exceeded ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Rui and Pi, ungrateful as dogs and horses and vicious as owls and jackals, secretly drew in the young and plotted this monstrous treason, violating heaven's order—their guilt deserved death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 叡結釁在心，陰構不息，間說戚蕃，擬窺乾象。

translations.literal: Rui bound enmity in his heart, secretly plotting without cease, going among the imperial kin to speak, intending to spy on the heavenly signs.
translations.idiomatic: Rui harbored enmity in his heart and plotted ceaselessly in secret, going among the imperial kin and intending to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 雖覩休平，未懷疑惑，何嘗片辭披露宿志，原心語跡，實為賊首。

translations.literal: Though he saw peace and prosperity, he did not harbor doubt; when had he ever in a single word disclosed his long-held intent? Judging by heart and words and traces, he was in truth the chief of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm was at peace, he never wavered in his intent and never disclosed it in the slightest word. Judging heart, speech, and acts together, he was truly the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 丕之二子，從惡累年，交扇東西，規擾并夏，測觀此狀，無容不知。

translations.literal: Pi's two sons followed evil for years, fanning each other east and west, planning to disturb Bing and Xia—judging from this pattern, he could not but have known.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's two sons followed evil for years, stirring trouble east and west and plotting to disturb Bing and Xia provinces—he cannot but have known.

sentences.zh: 雖聖慈含育，恕其生命，其若天地何！

translations.literal: Though Your Sacred Mercy nurtures and forgives their lives, what of Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Sacred Mercy would nurture and spare their lives, what of Heaven and Earth!

sentences.zh: 其若神祇何！

translations.literal: What of the spirits!
translations.idiomatic: What of the spirits!

sentences.zh: 夫効誠盡節，為下之恒分；

translations.literal: Devoting loyalty and fulfilling integrity is the constant duty of subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Devoting loyalty and fulfilling one's duty is the constant obligation of subjects;

sentences.zh: 刑茲無捨，在上之常法。

translations.literal: punishing such without leniency is the constant law of superiors.
translations.idiomatic: punishing such crimes without mercy is the constant law of rulers.

sentences.zh: 況曲蒙莫大之恩，奬以忠貞之義，而更違天背道，包藏姦逆，求情推理，罪乃常誅。

translations.literal: Moreover, having especially received immeasurable grace and been encouraged with loyal steadfastness, yet instead violating heaven and turning from the Way, harboring treachery and rebellion—in seeking sentiment and reasoning through the case, their crime warrants ordinary execution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, having received immeasurable grace and been encouraged to loyalty, yet violating heaven and the Way and harboring treachery—in law their crime warrants the ordinary death penalty.

sentences.zh: 而慈造寬渥，更流恩貸，續叡三斷之骸，還丕已絕之魄，二三縱宥，實虧憲典。

translations.literal: Yet Your Merciful Creation is broad and generous, further flowing grace in pardon—continuing Rui's thrice-severed body and restoring Pi's already-extinguished soul; two or three leniencies in truth impair the code of law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty's merciful grace flows in pardon—sparing Rui who deserved dismemberment and restoring Pi who deserved extinction; such repeated leniency truly impairs the code of law.

sentences.zh: 猶復上延天眷，言念疇日。

translations.literal: Still further extending heaven's favor, speaking of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Still further extending heaven's favor and speaking of former days.

sentences.zh: 不以臣等背負餘黨，別垂明詔，再申齊信之恩，重喻晈日之旨，伏讀悲慚，惟深愧惕。」

translations.literal: Not holding us as remnants of the faction, You separately issued a clear edict, again proclaiming the grace of mutual trust and reiterating the intent bright as day; bowing and reading it, we are grieved and ashamed, deeply awed and remorseful."
translations.idiomatic: Not treating us as remnants of the faction, You separately issued a clear edict again proclaiming mutual trust and reiterating pledges bright as day; reading it we are grieved and ashamed, filled with deep remorse and awe."

sentences.zh: 叡長子希道，字洪度，有風貌，美鬚髯。

translations.literal: Rui's eldest son Xidao, styled Hongdu, had a fine bearing and handsome beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's eldest son Xidao, styled Hongdu, had a distinguished bearing and a handsome beard.

sentences.zh: 歷覽經史，頗有文致。

translations.literal: He perused the classics and histories and had considerable literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and wrote with considerable polish.

sentences.zh: 初拜中散，遷通直郎，坐父事徙於遼西。

translations.literal: At first appointed Palace Attendant, he was transferred to Direct Attendant; owing to his father's affair he was relocated to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed palace attendant, then promoted to direct attendant; owing to his father's crime he was relocated to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 於後得還，從征自效。

translations.literal: Later he was permitted to return and followed campaigns to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was permitted to return and served in campaigns to prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 以軍功拜給事中，遷司徒記室、司空主簿。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Palace Attendant and transferred to Recorder of the Department of State Affairs and Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was appointed palace attendant, then transferred to recorder in the Department of State Affairs and chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍元英攻蕭衍司州，以希道為副，及克義陽，以功賜爵淮陽男。

translations.literal: General Who Campaigns South Yuan Ying attacked Xiao Yan's Si Province; Xidao served as his deputy, and when Yiyang was taken, for merit he was granted the title Baron of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When General Who Campaigns South Yuan Ying attacked Xiao Yan's Si Province, Xidao served as his deputy; when Yiyang was taken, he was granted the title baron of Huaiyang for his merit.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand master of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 以學關今古，參議新令。

translations.literal: Because his learning connected past and present, he participated in deliberating the new code.
translations.idiomatic: Because his learning spanned past and present, he participated in drafting the new legal code.

sentences.zh: 轉廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 加龍驤將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given the additional posts of Flying Dragon General and Governor of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed flying dragon general and governor of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: With his existing generalship he was transferred to Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his general's rank, he was transferred to governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 希道頻表辭免。

translations.literal: Xidao repeatedly submitted memorials declining and requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao repeatedly submitted memorials requesting dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又除東夏州刺史，不拜。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Governor of Eastern Xia Province but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed governor of Eastern Xia Province but declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 轉北中郎將，遷前將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Northern Palace Guard, then promoted to General of the Vanguard and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the northern palace guard, then promoted to general of the vanguard and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 希道善於馭邊，甚有威略，轉平西將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Xidao was skilled at governing the frontier and had great authority and strategy; he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao was skilled at governing the frontier and had great authority and strategic acumen; he was transferred to general who pacifies the west and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 正光四年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengguang he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the fourth year of Zhengguang.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title general who pacifies the army and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 希道有六子。

translations.literal: Xidao had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao had six sons.

sentences.zh: 士懋，字元偉。

translations.literal: Shimao, styled Yuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shimao, styled Yuanwei.

sentences.zh: 天平中，以其曾祖麗有翼戴之勳，詔特復鉅鹿郡開國公，邑三百戶，令士懋襲。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, because his great-grandfather Li had merit in supporting and enthroning the emperor, an edict specially restored the title Duke of Julu Commandery with a fief of three hundred households, ordering Shimao to inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era, because his great-grandfather Li had merit in supporting and enthroning the emperor, an edict specially restored the ducal title of Julu Commandery with a fief of three hundred households and ordered Shimao to inherit it.

sentences.zh: 武定中，平東將軍、營州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he served as general who pacifies the east and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 士懋弟士宗，字仲彥。

translations.literal: Shimao's younger brother Shizong, styled Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Shimao's younger brother Shizong, styled Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 尚書左外兵郎中。

translations.literal: Director of the Left Outer Military Affairs Section of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the left outer military affairs section of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 士宗弟士述，字幼文。

translations.literal: Shizong's younger brother Shishu, styled Youwen.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's younger brother Shishu, styled Youwen.

sentences.zh: 符璽郎中。

translations.literal: Director of Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 士宗、士述，建義初，並於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Shizong and Shishu, at the beginning of Jianyi, were both killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong and Shishu were both killed at Heyin at the beginning of Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 士述弟士沈，出繼從叔昕之。

translations.literal: Shishu's younger brother Shishen was given in adoption to succeed his father's younger cousin Xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu's younger brother Shishen was given in adoption to succeed his father's younger cousin Xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 士沈弟士廉，字季脩。

translations.literal: Shishen's younger brother Shilian, styled Jixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shishen's younger brother Shilian, styled Jixiu.

sentences.zh: 建州平北府長史。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-North Staff of Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of the pacify-the-north staff of Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 永安末，為尒朱世隆攻陷州城，見害。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an, when Erzhu Shilong captured and overran the provincial city, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an, when Erzhu Shilong captured the provincial city, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 士廉弟士佩，字季偉。

translations.literal: Shilian's younger brother Shipi, styled Jiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's younger brother Shipi, styled Jiwei.

sentences.zh: 武定中，安東將軍、司州治中。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, General Who Pacifies the East and Chief Administrator of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he served as general who pacifies the east and chief administrator of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 希道弟希悅，尚書外兵郎中、驃騎諮議參軍、通直散騎常侍、平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Xidao's younger brother Xiyue served as Director of Outer Military Affairs in the Ministry of Works, Consultant to the General of Fast Cavalry, Direct Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General Who Pacifies the South, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao's younger brother Xiyue served as director of outer military affairs in the Ministry of Works, consultant to the general of fast cavalry, direct regular attendant of the scattered riders, general who pacifies the south, and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General of the Guard, and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted regular attendant of the scattered riders, general of the guard, and governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 希悅弟希謐，太尉參軍，早卒。

translations.literal: Xiyue's younger brother Ximi, staff officer under the Grand Commander, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyue's younger brother Ximi, a staff officer under the grand commander, died young.

sentences.zh: 希謐弟希靜，字季默。

translations.literal: Ximi's younger brother Xijing, styled Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: Ximi's younger brother Xijing, styled Jimo.

sentences.zh: 司徒默曹，稍遷邵郡太守。

translations.literal: Clerk in the Silent Office of the Department of State Affairs; gradually promoted to Governor of Shao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as clerk in the silent office of the Department of State Affairs and was gradually promoted to governor of Shao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 希靜弟希質，字幼成。

translations.literal: Xijing's younger brother Xizhi, styled Youcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing's younger brother Xizhi, styled Youcheng.

sentences.zh: 起家員外郎，領侍御史，稍遷散騎侍郎、陽城太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as Vice Director and concurrently served as Attendant Censor; gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Scattered Riders and Governor of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as vice director and concurrently served as attendant censor, gradually rising to gentleman of the scattered riders and governor of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除龍驤將軍、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed Flying Dragon General and Governor of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed flying dragon general and governor of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將率眾數萬從郁洲浮海據島，來侵州界，希質討破之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent a general leading tens of thousands to float from sea at Yuzhou and occupy an island, invading the provincial border; Xizhi attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent a general with an army of tens of thousands to sail from Yuzhou and seize an island, invading the provincial border; Xizhi attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 轉建州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Jian Province, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Jian Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，世隆率眾北還晉陽，希質固守拒之，城陷，兄子被害。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong led troops north back to Jinyang; Xizhi held firm and resisted, but when the city fell his brother's son was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong led troops north to Jinyang; Xizhi held the city and resisted, but when it fell his brother's son was killed.

sentences.zh: 希質妻元氏，榮妻之兄孫，由是獲免。

translations.literal: Xizhi's wife was of the Yuan clan, granddaughter of Rong's wife's elder brother; by this he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi's wife was a Yuan, granddaughter of Erzhu Rong's wife's elder brother; by this connection he was spared.

sentences.zh: 天平初，給事黃門侍郎，遷魏尹，轉太常卿、衞大將軍、都官尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; transferred to Intendant of Wei; then Director of the Court of Sacrifices, Grand General of the Guard, and Minister of Judgment Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he served as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, then as intendant of Wei, then as director of the court of sacrifices, grand general of the guard, and minister of judgment affairs.

sentences.zh: 武定七年夏卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Wuding he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the seventh year of Wuding, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、中書監、青州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Governor of Qing Province; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted grand general of fast cavalry, supervisor of the secretariat, and governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 希質名家子，位宦又通，不能平心於物，唯與山偉、宇文忠之等共為朋黨，排毀朝俊，有識者薄之。

translations.literal: Xizhi was a son of an eminent house, and his offices were high as well; he could not be even-minded toward others, but only formed a faction with Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, and others, driving away and slandering outstanding men of the court—those with discernment looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi was a son of an eminent house who rose to high office, yet he could not treat others fairly; he formed a faction with Shan Wei, Yuwen Zhongzhi, and others, driving out and slandering worthy officials of the court, and those with discernment looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 子珣，字子琰。

translations.literal: His son Xun, styled Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, styled Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 開府參軍。

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the General Who Opens a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of a general who opens a commandery.

sentences.zh: 次瑾，字子瑜。

translations.literal: Next, Jin, styled Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Jin, styled Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 性並粗險，乃為劫盜，珣、瑾俱死。

translations.literal: Both by nature were crude and ruthless; they became bandits, and Xun and Jin both died.
translations.idiomatic: Both were crude and violent by nature; they turned to banditry, and Xun and Jin both died.

sentences.zh: 瑾弟瓘，字子璧。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Guan, styled Zibi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Guan, styled Zibi.

sentences.zh: 次悉達。

translations.literal: Next, Xida.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Xida.

sentences.zh: 武定中，並儀同開府參軍。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, both were Staff Officers of the General with the Honorary Title of the Three Excellencies Who Opens a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era both served as staff officers of generals with the honorary title of the three excellencies who open a commandery.

sentences.zh: 麗弟頹，早卒。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Tui died early.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Tui died young.

sentences.zh: 子□，字清都。

translations.literal: His son □, styled Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: His son □, styled Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 性機巧，歷位長水校尉，賜爵廣牧子。

translations.literal: In nature he was clever and resourceful; through successive offices he reached Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Waters and was granted the title Baron of Guangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resourceful by nature, he rose through the ranks to commandant of the ever-flowing waters and was enfeoffed as baron of Guangmu.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、游擊將軍、北中郎將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Flying Dragon General, Raiding General, and General of the Northern Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to flying dragon general, raiding general, and general of the northern palace guard.

sentences.zh: 轉南中郎將，帶魯陽太守，進號前將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Southern Palace Guard, concurrently serving as Prefect of Luyang, and advanced in rank to General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the southern palace guard, concurrently served as prefect of Luyang, and was advanced to general of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、夏州刺史，諡曰順。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded his former generalship and the governorship of Xia Province, with the posthumous name Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously awarded his former general's rank and the governorship of Xia Province, with the posthumous name Shun (Compliant).

sentences.zh: 頹弟陵成，中校尉、河間太守、祕書中散、新城子。

translations.literal: Tui's younger brother Lingcheng was Central Commandant, Prefect of Hejian, Attendant Cavalryman of the Secretariat, and Baron of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tui's younger brother Lingcheng served as central commandant, prefect of Hejian, attendant cavalryman of the secretariat, and baron of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 陵成弟龍成，有父兄之風。

translations.literal: Lingcheng's younger brother Longcheng had the manner of his father and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng's younger brother Longcheng took after his father and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 少以功臣子為中散，稍遷散騎常侍，賜爵永安子。

translations.literal: In youth, as the son of a meritorious official, he served as Attendant Cavalryman; gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; granted the title Baron of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man, through his status as a meritorious official's son, he entered service as an attendant cavalryman, was gradually promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and was enfeoffed as baron of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 加平遠將軍，出為安南將軍、青州刺史，假樂安公。

translations.literal: Given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Far; sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Qing Province, with the provisional title Duke of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional rank of general who pacifies the far, sent out as general who pacifies the south and governor of Qing Province, and granted the provisional title duke of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 愛民恤下，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: He loved the people and showed concern for subordinates; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the people and looked after his subordinates, and the common people praised him.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子昶，字細文，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chang, styled Xiwen, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang, courtesy name Xiwen, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 正始中，為太尉屬，加寧遠將軍，以本官行滎陽郡事。

translations.literal: During Zhengshi, he served on the staff of the Grand Commandant, was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Distant, and with his existing office charged with affairs of Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he served on the grand commandant's staff, was given the additional rank of general who pacifies the distant, and with his existing office administered Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 被劾，會赦免。

translations.literal: He was impeached, but an amnesty coincided and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached but was pardoned when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 久之，進號廣武將軍，遷司空司馬，尋拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After some time, he was advanced to General Who Displays Martial Might, transferred to Marshal of the Ministry of Works, and soon appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was advanced to general who displays martial might, transferred to marshal of the ministry of works, and soon appointed grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 昶無他才能，唯飲酒為事。

translations.literal: Chang had no other ability; drinking alone was his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had no other talents—drinking was his sole pursuit.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、京兆內史，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Intendant of Jingzhao, he firmly declined and would not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When he was offered the posts of general who pacifies the west and intendant of Jingzhao, he firmly declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 轉平北將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who pacifies the north and inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 入為衞將軍、大鴻臚卿，仍除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as General of the Guard and Minister Herald, then was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as general of the guard and minister herald, then appointed general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 天平中，進號驃騎大將軍，加散騎常侍、領左右、兼給事黃門侍郎，仍兼 太僕卿。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he was advanced to General of Chivalry and Cavalry, additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Left and Right, concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and still concurrently Minister of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was advanced to general of chivalry and cavalry, additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, director of the left and right, concurrently attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and continued to serve concurrently as minister of the stud.

sentences.zh: 復以本將軍為東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Again, with his existing generalship, he was made Governor of East Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed governor of East Xu Province with his existing general's rank.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、衞尉卿、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded his former generalship, Director of the Guard Office, and Governorship of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded his former general's rank, the directorship of the guard office, and the governorship of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 龍成季弟騏驎，侍御中散，[4]轉侍御長。

translations.literal: Longcheng's youngest brother Qilin served as Attendant Cavalryman-in-Attendance, [4] then was transferred to Chief of the Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Longcheng's youngest brother Qilin served as attendant cavalryman-in-attendance, [4] then was transferred to chief of the imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 太和初，新平太守、銀青光祿大夫，以彭城勳除夏州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Prefect of Xinping and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal; for merit at Pengcheng he was appointed Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he served as prefect of Xinping and grand master of splendid happiness with the silver seal; for his merit at Pengcheng he was appointed governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 子高貴，孝昌中，兗州鎮東府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Gaogui, during Xiaochang, served as staff member of the legal bureau in the Eastern Headquarters of Yan Province Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gaogui served during the Xiaochang era as staff member of the legal bureau in the eastern headquarters of the Yanzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 子操，武定末，度支尚書。

translations.literal: His son Cao, at the end of Wuding, was Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao served at the end of the Wuding era as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 操弟楚。

translations.literal: Cao's younger brother Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao's younger brother was Chu.

sentences.zh: 高貴弟順宗，員外郎、祕書中散。

translations.literal: Gaogui's younger brother Shunzong served as Outside Section Attendant and Attendant Cavalryman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaogui's younger brother Shunzong served as outside-section attendant and attendant cavalryman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子概之，武定末，東莞太守。

translations.literal: His son Gaizhi, at the end of Wuding, was Prefect of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gaizhi served at the end of the Wuding era as prefect of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 俟族弟宜，雲中鎮將。

translations.literal: Si's clansman younger brother Yi was Garrison Commander of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Si's clansman Yi served as garrison commander of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 子雋，高宗世，歷侍中、給事。

translations.literal: His son Jun, during the reign of Emperor Wencheng, successively served as Palace Attendant and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun served during Emperor Wencheng's reign as palace attendant and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，侍御長。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was Chief of the Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as chief of the imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 以謀誅乙渾，拜侍中、樂部尚書。

translations.literal: For plotting to execute Yifu Hun, he was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of the Music Section.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in the plot to execute Yifu Hun, he was appointed palace attendant and minister of the music section.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、吏部尚書，賜爵安樂公，甚見委任。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Personnel, granted the title Duke of Anle, and greatly entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and minister of personnel, enfeoffed as duke of Anle, and placed in great trust.

sentences.zh: 尋拜尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後除安東將軍、定州刺史，轉征東大將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ding Province, then transferred to General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed general who pacifies the east and inspector of Ding Province, then transferred to general who campaigns east and inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬惠，民吏安定。

translations.literal: His administration emphasized lenience and generosity; officials and people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: His governance favored lenience and generosity, and officials and people alike lived in security.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡貞公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Duke of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title duke of Zhen (Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 子登，澄城太守。

translations.literal: His son Deng was Prefect of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deng served as prefect of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 子匡，司空倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Kuang was staff member of the granary bureau in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuang served as staff member of the granary bureau in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 登弟子景元，元象初，衞將軍、儀同三司、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: Deng's nephew Jingyuan, at the beginning of Yuanxiang, was General of the Guard, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's nephew Jingyuan, at the beginning of the Yuanxiang era, served as general of the guard, equal in honor to the three excellencies, and governor of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陸俟威略智器有過人者。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Lu Si's authority, strategy, and native capacity exceeded those of ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Lu Si's martial authority, strategic skill, and native gifts surpassed those of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 馛識幹明厲，不替家風。

translations.literal: Ba was wise, capable, bright, and stern, never falling short of the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was wise, capable, and resolute, never falling short of the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 麗忠國奉主，為時梁棟，蹈忠履義，制於一豎。

translations.literal: Li was loyal to the state and devoted to his sovereign, a pillar of the age; he trod loyalty and fulfilled righteousness—yet was brought low by a single eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Li was loyal to the state and devoted to his sovereign, a pillar of his age who lived by loyalty and righteousness—yet was destroyed by a single eunuch.

sentences.zh: 惜哉！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: What a pity!

sentences.zh: 叡、琇以沉雅顯達，而釁逆陷禍。

translations.literal: Rui and Xiu, though refined and elegant and risen to prominence, were ruined through rebellion and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Xiu, though refined and already risen to eminence, were destroyed by treason.

sentences.zh: 深山大澤，實有龍蛇。

translations.literal: Deep mountains and great marshes truly harbor dragons and serpents.
translations.idiomatic: Deep mountains and great marshes truly harbor dragons and serpents.

sentences.zh: 希道風度有聲，子彰令終之美也。

translations.literal: Xidao was renowned for his bearing and grace; Zizhang embodied the beauty of a good end.
translations.idiomatic: Xidao was renowned for his bearing and grace; Zizhang fulfilled the ideal of a good end.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes.

sentences.zh: 安定盧水劉超等聚黨萬餘以叛 諸本「水」作「永」。

translations.literal: Collation note on 'Liu Chao and others of the Luishui [Hu] of Anding gathered a party of more than ten thousand and rebelled': in various editions 'water' (shui) is written as 'Yong' (yong).
translations.idiomatic: On "Liu Chao and others of the Luishui [Hu] of Anding gathered a party of more than ten thousand and rebelled": various editions read "Yong" instead of "water" (shui).

sentences.zh: 北史卷二八陸俟傳作「水」，通鑑卷一二四

translations.literal: The biography of Lu Si in Northern History, scroll 28, reads 'water' (shui); Comprehensive Mirror, scroll 124
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Lu Si in the Northern History (scroll 28) reads shui; the Comprehensive Mirror (scroll 124)

sentences.zh: 〈三九二八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3928〉

sentences.zh: 「水」下更有「胡」字。

translations.literal: After 'water' (shui) there is additionally the character 'Hu.'
translations.idiomatic: After shui the text also has the character hu (Hu).

sentences.zh: 按盧水胡屢見後漢書、三國志、晉書等史籍。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Luishui Hu appear repeatedly in the Book of Later Han, Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Jin, and other historical works.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: the Luishui Hu appear repeatedly in the Book of Later Han, Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Jin, and other histories.

sentences.zh: 若作「永」，則是人名，但下文只稱「超」等。

translations.literal: If written as 'Yong,' it would be a personal name, but below he is called only 'Chao' and the like.
translations.idiomatic: If read as Yong it would imply a personal name, yet the text below refers only to Chao and the others.

sentences.zh: 知「永」乃「水」之形訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Knowing that 'Yong' is a graphic corruption of 'water' (shui), it is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yong is clearly a graphic corruption of shui; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 與度世子淵婚親相好 諸本「淵」作「泉」。

translations.literal: Collation note on 'was on good terms by marriage with Yuan, son of Dushi': in various editions 'Yuan' (yuan) is written as 'Quan' (quan).
translations.idiomatic: On "was on good terms by marriage with Yuan, son of Dushi": various editions read Quan instead of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 按盧淵，卷四七有傳。

translations.literal: Commentary: Lu Yuan has a biography in scroll 47.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Lu Yuan has a biography in scroll 47.

sentences.zh: 這裏當是唐人避諱改，今回改。

translations.literal: Here it should be a change made by Tang people for taboo avoidance; it is now restored.
translations.idiomatic: This is plainly a Tang-era taboo alteration; the original reading is restored.

sentences.zh: 娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女 諸本無「東」字，北史卷二八陸叡傳有。

translations.literal: Collation note on 'he married a daughter of Cui Jian of Boling, Inspector of East Xu Province': various editions lack the character 'East'; the biography of Lu Rui in Northern History, scroll 28, has it.
translations.idiomatic: On "he married a daughter of Cui Jian of Boling, inspector of East Xu Province": most editions omit East; the biography of Lu Rui in the Northern History (scroll 28) includes it.

sentences.zh: 按下明云：「叡婚自東徐還。

translations.literal: Comment: Below it clearly states: 'Rui returned from his marriage in East Xu.'
translations.idiomatic: Comment: the text below explicitly states, "Rui returned from his marriage journey in East Xu."

sentences.zh: 」卷六二李彪傳稱陸叡「娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女」。

translations.literal: Biography of Li Biao, scroll 62, states regarding Lu Rui: 'he married a daughter of Cui Jian of Boling, Inspector of East Xu Province.'
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Li Biao (scroll 62) states that Lu Rui "married a daughter of Cui Jian of Boling, inspector of East Xu Province."

sentences.zh: 卷四九崔鑒傳也只稱鑒「出為奮威將軍、東徐州刺史」，不云「徐州」。

translations.literal: The biography of Cui Jian, scroll 49, likewise calls Jian only 'went out as General of Strenuous Might and Inspector of East Xu Province,' not saying 'Xu Province.'
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Cui Jian (scroll 49) likewise records only that Jian "went out as general of strenuous might and inspector of East Xu Province," not Xu Province alone.

sentences.zh: 此傳脫「東」字，今據補。

translations.literal: This biography omits the character 'East'; it is now supplied on evidence.
translations.idiomatic: This biography has dropped the character East; it is supplied on the evidence cited.

sentences.zh: 侍御中散 諸本「御」作「郎」，北史卷二八作「御」。

translations.literal: Collation note on 'Attendant Cavalryman-in-Attendance': in various editions 'attendant' (yu) is written as 'gentleman' (lang); Northern History, scroll 28, reads 'attendant' (yu).
translations.idiomatic: On "attendant cavalryman-in-attendance": various editions read lang (gentleman) instead of yu (attendant); the Northern History (scroll 28) reads yu.

sentences.zh: 按「侍御中散」魏初已有此官，太和後品令在從五品上。

translations.literal: Commentary: The office of Attendant Cavalryman-in-Attendance already existed in early Wei; after Taihe the rank regulations place it at upper fifth rank, subordinate grade.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: the office of attendant cavalryman-in-attendance existed as early as the founding of Wei; after Taihe the rank regulations place it at upper fifth rank, subordinate grade.

sentences.zh: 「侍郎中散」無此官名，今據改。

translations.literal: 'Attendant-Gentleman Cavalryman-in-Attendance' is not an existing office title; it is now emended on evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-gentleman cavalryman-in-attendance is not a valid office title; the text is emended accordingly.
